# Sawari: Hyderabad driving simulator

> Sawari is a free 3D driving simulator that runs in a web browser on phones, tablets, laptops and PCs. It recreates five real Hyderabad (Telangana, India) routes from OpenStreetMap and elevation data, with left-hand traffic, a right-hand-drive car, traffic signals, local traffic (autos, buses, two-wheelers), pedestrians, spoken turn-by-turn directions and a debrief that scores each drive and explains every fault. It is for practice and does not replace driving lessons or the RTA test.

Key facts:
- Name: Sawari (Urdu for "a ride"); tagline "Drive Hyderabad". Website: https://sawari.airacode.online/
- Made by: AiraCode Technologies (https://airacode.online)
- Price: free; no download, no sign-up; plays at https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html
- Devices: phones and tablets (held sideways, on-screen steering wheel and GO/BRAKE pedals), laptops and desktops (keyboard or gamepad)
- Routes (5, 18.8 km in all): Tank Bund Road (1.7 km, easy), Necklace Road (5.0 km, easy), Charminar and Pathergatti (2.1 km, hard), Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills (7.4 km, medium), Banjara Hills Road No. 1 (2.6 km, medium)
- Car: automatic gearbox with ABS; chase view or driver's seat; morning, midday, evening and night
- Rules checked: speeding, keeping left, wrong way on one-way roads, leaving the road, red lights, collisions, speed breakers taken too fast, turns without an indicator
- Sharing: a score card picture after each drive and a "challenge a friend" link with the score to beat
- Languages: website in English, Hindi, Urdu and Telugu; blog (63 articles) in English
- Data: map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); terrain from open terrain tiles
- Not affiliated with the Telangana Transport Department (RTA) or the traffic police

# Banjara Hills Road No. 1 driving guide: the climb from Masab Tank

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/banjara-hills-road-no-1-driving-guide.html
Category: Route guides · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Banjara Hills Road No. 1 is one of the busiest arterial roads in central Hyderabad, and it climbs steadily uphill from Masab Tank. The layout is simple, a divided road with no turns needed to follow it, but the signals come thick and fast, buses and autos stop without warning, and you will often be queuing on a slope.

This guide covers what driving on Road No. 1 is really like, when it is busiest, the hazards that catch people out, and how to rehearse it in Sawari before you drive it for real.

## What Banjara Hills Road No. 1 is like

### Layout and lanes

Road No. 1 starts near Masab Tank and heads north through Banjara Hills. For most of its length it is a divided road, with a median and two to three lanes in each direction depending on the stretch. Lanes narrow and widen as you go, sometimes with little warning, and the left lane is often partly taken up by stopped buses, autos and cars waiting to turn into side roads and buildings.

Road No. 1 is the first of the numbered roads that criss-cross Banjara Hills, and many of its junctions are with other numbered roads and colony streets. Some are signalled; others are simple gaps where vehicles nose out into the traffic.

### The climb

Banjara Hills sits higher than the land around Masab Tank, and Road No. 1 climbs to reach it. The gradient is gentle but long. In Sawari's terrain data the road rises by around 35 metres over the first two kilometres before dropping away again near the end. You feel it most when you are stopped at a signal partway up and need to move off without rolling back.

### Landmarks

The road is lined with offices, hospitals, hotels, restaurants and shops. In its busier second half you pass well-known names such as the City Center mall, the Taj Krishna hotel and GVK One. The route in Sawari finishes near Vengal Rao Park.

## When Road No. 1 is busiest

Weekday mornings and evenings bring heavy office traffic through Banjara Hills, as people travel between the older city, Punjagutta, Jubilee Hills and HITEC City. Through the day there is a steady flow of cabs, autos and delivery riders.

Evenings and weekends add shoppers, diners and visitors to the malls and restaurants, with queues to get into car parks and cabs stopping at the gates. Early mornings, especially at weekends, are usually the calmest time for a first drive. Rain slows everything further; our monsoon driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/monsoon-driving-hyderabad.html) explains what changes.

## Hazards on Banjara Hills Road No. 1

### Signals close together

Signals come one after another, so you are often stopping, starting and queuing. Look well ahead to see what the next signal is doing, ease off early rather than braking hard, and stop at the line on red. Amber is not a reason to speed up, especially uphill, where a heavy vehicle behind you may struggle to stop.

### Moving off on the slope

Queues on an uphill stretch mean hill starts. The car in front may roll back a little as it moves off, so leave a gap of a car's length or so when you stop. In a manual, use the handbrake or the biting point rather than slipping the clutch for long periods. In an automatic, move your foot smoothly from brake to accelerator.

### Buses and autos stopping

Buses stop at the kerb and autos pull over whenever someone waves. In the left lane, expect the vehicle ahead to stop with little warning. Before you move out around it, check over your shoulder and in your mirrors for bikes coming up on your right. Our guide to sharing the road with autos, buses and two-wheelers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) covers this in detail.

### Mall, hotel and hospital entrances

Cars slow down to turn into car parks and hotel driveways, and others nose out to join the traffic. Watch for indicators and for drivers who forget them, and do not block an entrance when you queue.

### Two-wheelers and pedestrians

Bikes filter through queues at every signal and move across lanes as gaps open. People cross between stopped vehicles, particularly near bus stops and shops. When traffic is crawling, watch the gaps between cars as well as the road ahead.

### Speed breakers on side roads

If you turn off Road No. 1 into a colony road, expect speed breakers soon after the junction, and not always painted ones. See speed breakers and speed limits in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/speed-breakers-speed-limits-hyderabad.html).

## Practical tips for driving Road No. 1

- **Settle in the middle lane** where there are three, away from stopping buses on the left and turning traffic on the right.

- **Look two signals ahead.** It helps you slow down smoothly instead of braking late.

- **Practise hill starts somewhere quiet first.** A gentle slope in an empty lane is a better place to learn than a queue at a busy signal.

- **Signal every lane change.** With traffic this dense, early indicators help everyone.

- **Follow the posted speed limits.** The signs set your speed, not the car overtaking you.

- **Keep calm in queues.** Horns and lane changes rarely save time here.

If you are new to the city, our guide to driving in Hyderabad for beginners (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-beginners.html) is a good place to start, and the Hyderabad traffic rules guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-traffic-rules-guide.html) covers the rules you will be expected to follow.

## Practise Banjara Hills Road No. 1 in Sawari

Sawari's Banjara Hills Road No. 1 route (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html#banjara-hills) is a 2.6 km uphill drive from Masab Tank. It has no turns to make, but it is rated Medium because of the climb, the busy junctions and the buses and autos stopping along the way.

- **Pick a time and traffic level.** Start with light traffic in the morning, then build up to Dense to see the queues form at the signals.

- **Follow the blue route band.** It shows your lane on the route. Keep the car inside it and left of the centre line.

- **Feel the climb.** The terrain comes from real elevation data, and the car's physics respond to it: you need a little more throttle uphill, and the car carries speed downhill near the end. The car in Sawari is a six-speed automatic, so it is good practice for smooth brake-to-accelerator starts, though not for clutch control.

- **Stop at the line on red.** Running a red is the heaviest fault in the debrief. If you cross on amber, a warning reminds you to be ready to stop next time.

- **Use `Q` and `E`** for the indicators whenever you change lanes around stopped buses.

- **Switch views with `C`.** The driver's seat view is closer to what you will really see. The car has no mirrors, so drag the mouse to look around before you move across.

The debrief lists every fault with advice: red lights, speeding, collisions, drifting right of the centre line, leaving the road, speed breakers taken too fast and missed indicators. Your best score on the route is saved in your browser, so you can see yourself improve. Press `R` if you need to return to the route.

You can start the Road No. 1 drive here (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=banjara-hills), free in Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop, with touch controls, a keyboard or a gamepad.

## In the simulator vs the real road

The road layout, lane counts, median, signals and the climb in Sawari come from OpenStreetMap and satellite terrain data, so the shape of the drive is real. Much of the roadside is estimated. Building facades and Banjara Hills villas are generated to look typical of the area, and speed breakers, U-turn openings, stalls, parked vehicles, hoardings and most street lamps are placed by rule. Signal timings are the game's own, and the speed limit shown comes from map data rather than the sign on the day.

Use the simulator to rehearse the habits this road asks for: smooth stops and starts, early signals and patience in traffic. On the real road, follow the actual signs, signals and traffic police.

Sawari is for practice only. It does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor, and it cannot teach clutch control or real hill starts in a manual car.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Banjara Hills Road No. 1 steep?**
It is a steady climb rather than a steep hill. The road rises gradually from Masab Tank for most of its length, which matters most when you are stopped in a queue on the slope and have to move off again.

**When is Road No. 1 in Banjara Hills busiest?**
Weekday office hours are busy, and evenings and weekends add shoppers heading to the malls and restaurants along the road. Early mornings are usually the calmest time to drive it.

**How do I stop rolling back on an uphill signal?**
In a manual car, hold the car on the handbrake or footbrake, bring the clutch up to the biting point and release the brake as you add a little power. In an automatic, move your foot smoothly from brake to accelerator. Leave a good gap to the car in front in case it rolls back.

**Can I practise Banjara Hills Road No. 1 online?**
Yes. Sawari has a free Road No. 1 route from Masab Tank, built on real map and terrain data, that runs in your browser on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop. It is practice only and does not replace driving lessons.

# Driving to Charminar: an Old City driving guide to Charminar Road and Pathergatti

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/charminar-old-city-driving-guide.html
Category: Route guides · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Driving near Charminar is the most demanding short drive in Hyderabad: narrow one-way streets, a circle round the monument, shoppers and handcarts at the kerb, and autos and two-wheelers in every gap. It is very manageable at walking pace and with patience, but it rewards preparation, and it is no place for a first drive.

This guide covers the Old City roads around the Charminar and Pathergatti, when they are busiest, what catches drivers out, where parking fits in, and how to rehearse the route in Sawari before you go.

## What the roads around Charminar are like

The Charminar, built in the late sixteenth century under the Qutb Shahi dynasty, stands at the centre of the Old City, where the main streets meet. The Mecca Masjid is close by to the south-west, the bangle shops of Laad Bazaar run off to the west, and to the north the road passes Gulzar Houz and continues as Pathergatti, with its long arcade of stone-fronted shops.

### Layout and lanes

Around the monument the streets are mostly one-way, and many are only one or two cars wide once you allow for parked two-wheelers, shop goods and handcarts. Traffic moves round the Charminar itself rather than past it, so you need to know which exit you want before you arrive. Lane markings are scarce; your real lane is whatever space is left between the kerb and the vehicles beside you.

Pathergatti Road is wider and busier, a main shopping street lined with arched shopfronts. The ground falls gently as you head north towards the river Musi, so on a crowded street you will be covering the brake more than the accelerator.

### One-way rules

Because so many streets are one-way, the direct route is often not the legal one. You may need to loop through side lanes to reach a street you can see straight ahead. One-way arrangements around the Old City can also change with works, events and traffic management, so follow the signs on the day rather than an old memory of the route.

## When Charminar and the Old City are busiest

The Old City wakes later than the rest of Hyderabad. Early morning, before shutters go up, is usually the calmest time to drive. From late morning the shops open, deliveries arrive and the crowds build, and by evening the streets around the Charminar are packed.

Weekends and holidays bring tourists as well as shoppers. Festival seasons are busier still. During Ramzan the area round the Charminar becomes a night market, and the streets are full late into the night. Muharram, Bonalu and other festivals bring processions and diversions. If you need to drive at these times, check Hyderabad Traffic Police (https://www.htp.gov.in) advisories first, or leave the car behind.

## Hazards when driving near Charminar

### People everywhere

Pedestrians are the main traffic here. Shoppers step off the footpath to get round goods and parked bikes, people cross wherever they like, and visitors stop in the road to take photographs of the monument. Drive at a speed where you could stop within a car's length, and keep looking at the footpaths as well as the road.

### Two-wheelers and autos

Bikes and scooters squeeze past on both sides and cut in front at the circle. Autos stop dead to pick up and drop off. Hold a steady, predictable line; do not make sudden moves to block a bike, and do not assume the vehicle ahead will keep going. Our guide to sharing the road with autos, buses and two-wheelers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) has more on this.

### Stalls, handcarts and parked vehicles

Goods spill out of shops, fruit and flower carts stop at the kerb, and parked two-wheelers line both sides. That narrows the road and hides people about to step out. Keep a gap of at least a door's width from parked vehicles where you can, and watch for a foot or a wheel appearing between them.

### The circle round the monument

Traffic round the Charminar behaves like a busy roundabout with little lane discipline. Approach slowly, give way to vehicles already going round, signal your exit, and expect bikes to pass on your left as you leave. The general rules in our guide to driving roundabouts in India (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/roundabouts-how-to-drive-india.html) apply, but here everything happens at walking pace.

### Speed breakers

Old City streets have many speed breakers, and not all are painted. Watch for vehicles ahead dipping and take every hump slowly and straight on.

## Charminar parking and practical tips

- **Think about whether to drive at all.** For a visit to the Charminar, many people find it easier to come by auto, cab or bus and walk the last part.

- **Park only where it is signed.** Space near the monument is very limited. Never park on the carriageway, across a lane or in front of a shop entrance; it blocks traffic and you may be towed or fined.

- **Know your route before you set off.** With one-way streets, a wrong turn can cost you a long loop. Check it beforehand rather than reading a phone in traffic.

- **Go slowly and keep going.** A steady crawl is easier for everyone to read than stop-start jerks.

- **Use the horn sparingly.** A short tap to say you are there is enough; long blasts do not clear a crowded street.

- **Take an experienced driver with you** the first time you drive here.

## Practise the Charminar route in Sawari

Sawari's Charminar and Pathergatti route (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html#charminar) is a 2.1 km drive up Charminar Road from the south, round the Charminar itself, then north to Pathergatti Road. It is the hardest of the five routes: nine turns in two kilometres, including a short loop through side lanes because of the way the one-way streets are mapped.

- **Drive it with no traffic first.** Set traffic to None and learn the turns. Follow the blue route band, which always shows the legal direction on one-way streets, and listen for the spoken directions.

- **Signal every turn.** Press `Q` for left or `E` for right well before the turn. The indicator cancels itself afterwards. Turning without one is logged in your debrief.

- **Use the driver's seat view.** Press `C` to switch from the chase view. Judging gaps from the driver's seat is harder, and closer to the real thing. Drag the mouse to look round corners and at the circle before you join it.

- **Add traffic.** Raise the traffic level step by step. At Dense, autos, scooters and motorbikes crowd the streets and the circle round the monument gets busy.

- **Try it at night.** The night setting lights the streets with lamps and lit windows, and every vehicle has head and tail lamps. Switch your own headlights on with `L`.

The debrief at the end gives you a score and every fault with advice: collisions with vehicles, pedestrians, walls or buildings, going the wrong way on a one-way street, running a red light, taking speed breakers too fast, leaving the road and missed indicators. If you take a wrong turn, press `R` to return to the route.

If this route feels too much at first, that is normal. Build up on Tank Bund Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/tank-bund-road-driving-guide.html) and Necklace Road, then come back. You can start the Charminar drive here (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=charminar), free on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop.

## In the simulator vs the real road

The streets, their widths and their one-way directions in Sawari come from OpenStreetMap, and the Charminar is modelled as a landmark at its real position. Much of the street life is estimated. Stalls, parked two-wheelers, hoardings, speed breakers, most street lamps and many facades are placed by rule to look typical of the Old City, not copied from the real street. The game also cannot show the current vehicle restrictions around the monument, which can change.

So practise the skills, not the exact street: slow speed, wide awareness, early signals and patience at the circle. On the day, follow the real signs and the traffic police.

Sawari is for practice only. It does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor. The Old City is not a place for your first real drive; go with an experienced driver until you are confident.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can you drive right up to the Charminar?**
Vehicle access around the monument has been restricted in recent years as parts of the area were made pedestrian-friendly, and the rules can change. Follow the signs and the traffic police on the day, and expect to park some distance away and walk.

**Is there parking near Charminar?**
Space close to the monument is very limited and is often taken early, especially at weekends and during festivals. Use only places signed for parking, never the carriageway or a shop front, or come by auto, cab or bus and walk the last stretch.

**What is the best time to drive in the Old City?**
Early morning, before the shops open, is usually the calmest. Late mornings, evenings, weekends, festival days and Ramzan nights are much busier, with heavy crowds on foot around the Charminar.

**Is the Charminar route hard for beginners?**
It is the hardest of Sawari's five routes: narrow one-way streets, a circle round the monument and nine turns in about two kilometres. Practise the easier lakeside routes first, and drive the real streets with an experienced driver beside you.

# HITEC City to Jubilee Hills: driving the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, Road No. 45 and Road No. 36

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hitec-city-to-jubilee-hills-drive.html
Category: Route guides · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

The drive from HITEC City to Jubilee Hills takes you from the Cyber Towers office district, past Inorbit Mall, across the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge and along Road No. 45 and Road No. 36 to Jubilee Hills Checkpost. It is only about seven kilometres, but it packs in wide IT-corridor roads, lane choices before the bridge, and busy signals at the Jubilee Hills end.

This guide walks through the route section by section, explains when it is busiest and what to watch for, and shows how to rehearse it in Sawari, the free browser driving simulator on real Hyderabad roads.

## The route, section by section

### Cyber Towers and HITEC City Road

You start in the heart of HITEC City, by Cyber Towers, and head south along HITEC City Road. This is a wide divided road, several lanes each way, built for office traffic. You pass Cyber Gateway, the metro line overhead near Raidurg station, and the Mindspace junction. Signals here are big, multi-lane junctions where lanes for turning and going straight are separated early, so read the overhead signs and the road markings as you approach.

### Inorbit Mall and the bridge approach

Near Inorbit Mall the route bears left onto Inorbit Mall Road. This is where traffic from the mall, from side roads and from the main road all meet, and where you need to be in the right lane for the approach to the bridge. Cabs pull in to pick up passengers, and drivers who have left their lane choice late cut across. Get into position early and hold it.

### The Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge

The cable-stayed bridge over Durgam Cheruvu lake is one of the newer landmarks of Hyderabad. Its towers and fan of cables are striking by day, and at night the bridge is lit up in colour.

The drive across is short and straightforward, but the view draws attention. Some drivers slow down to look or take photos, so watch the brake lights ahead and keep a good gap. Do not stop on the bridge. The bridge has at times been closed to vehicles at weekends so that people can walk across it; check the latest advisories before planning a drive at those times.

### Road No. 45 and Road No. 36 to Jubilee Hills Checkpost

On the Jubilee Hills side the route follows Road No. 45, a narrower road with openings in the median, past homes, restaurants and offices. The ground rises gently as you head east, in keeping with the rocky, hilly character of Jubilee Hills. A couple of turns bring you on to Road No. 36, a busy commercial road with the metro viaduct overhead, shops and showrooms on both sides and a run of signals. The route finishes at Jubilee Hills Checkpost, one of the busiest junctions in this part of the city.

## When HITEC City to Jubilee Hills traffic is heaviest

This corridor follows office hours more closely than almost anywhere in Hyderabad. Weekday mornings and evenings, when people arrive at and leave the IT parks, are the busiest, and many offices work shifts, so traffic can build at unexpected times too.

Weekends are different rather than quiet. Office traffic drops, but Inorbit Mall, the restaurants on Road No. 36 and the cable bridge itself draw crowds, particularly in the evening. Rain slows everything down; see our monsoon driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/monsoon-driving-hyderabad.html).

## Hazards on the cable bridge route

### Late lane changes

Wide roads with lane choices and ramps tempt drivers into last-second moves across several lanes. Do not join them. If you find yourself in the wrong lane, carry on and find a safe way back rather than cutting across. Our guide to driving on flyovers in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-on-flyovers-hyderabad.html) covers how to handle ramps and merges.

### Cabs, shuttles and buses

Office cabs and company shuttles stop to drop and collect passengers, often near IT park gates and bus stops, and city buses pull in and out. Expect the vehicle ahead to stop suddenly, and check beside you before you pull out around it.

### Two-wheelers and delivery riders

Bikes filter through queues at every signal and move between lanes on the open stretches. Delivery riders in a hurry are common around HITEC City and Road No. 36. Hold a steady line, signal clearly and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

### Signals on Road No. 36

The signals on Road No. 36 come one after another, and the junctions are busy with turning traffic. Stop at the line on red, do not speed up for amber, and watch for pedestrians crossing at the junctions and under the metro.

### Median openings on Road No. 45

Vehicles slow in the right lane to turn or U-turn through the median. If a car ahead slows near an opening, assume it is turning.

## Practical tips for the drive

- **Know your lanes before you start.** The trickiest moments are lane choices near Inorbit Mall and the turns towards Road No. 36. Check the route before you leave rather than while driving.

- **Signal early.** On wide roads, indicate well before you move, so drivers in other lanes have time to see it. See indicators and lane discipline (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/indicators-and-lane-discipline.html).

- **Follow the posted limits.** Wide roads feel fast; the signs, not the traffic around you, set your speed.

- **Enjoy the bridge as a passenger.** The driver's job is the car in front.

- **Allow time at peak hours.** A short route can take a long time in office traffic, and rushing causes most mistakes.

## Practise HITEC City to Jubilee Hills in Sawari

Sawari's Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills route (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html#hitec-city) is a 7.4 km drive with ten turns: HITEC City Road, Inorbit Mall Road, the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, Road No. 45 and Road No. 36 to Jubilee Hills Checkpost. It is rated Medium, a good step up after the lakeside routes.

- **Learn the route with little traffic.** Follow the blue route band, which shows your lane, and turn on the spoken directions if you like hearing the next turn in advance.

- **Practise your lane choice.** Watch where the band leads before the bridge approach and get across early, with an indicator: `Q` for left, `E` for right. Turning without signalling is logged as a fault.

- **Raise the traffic level.** At Dense you will meet buses stopping, bikes filtering through gaps and queues at signals, much as you would on a weekday evening.

- **Drive it at night.** Choose the night setting to see the bridge, the street lamps and the vehicle lights. Switch your headlights on with `L`. Our night driving tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/night-driving-hyderabad-tips.html) apply here too.

- **Switch views with `C`.** The chase view helps you learn the turns; the driver's seat is closer to the real thing. The car has no mirrors, so drag the mouse to look around before lane changes.

The debrief at the end gives you a score out of 100 and lists every fault with advice: red lights, speeding, missed indicators, drifting right of the centre line, going the wrong way on a one-way section, collisions and speed breakers taken too fast. Your best score on the route is saved in your browser. If you go wrong, press `R` to return to the route.

Ready to try it? Drive the cable bridge route now (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=hitec-city). It runs in Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop, with touch controls, a keyboard or a gamepad.

## In the simulator vs the real road

The road layout, lane counts, flyover and bridge heights, signals and the gradients in Sawari come from OpenStreetMap and terrain data, and the bridge's towers stand where the real ones do. Much of the detail around them is estimated: building facades, the glass towers' exact shapes, speed breakers, U-turn openings, stalls, parked vehicles, hoardings and most street lamps are placed by rule. Signal timings are the game's own. The speed limit shown comes from map data and may not match the sign on the day.

Use the drive to practise habits, especially early lane choice and signalling, then follow the real signs, signals and traffic police on the road.

Sawari is for practice only. It does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor, and its scores do not reflect any official test.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can you stop on the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge to take photos?**
Do not stop on the carriageway. Stopping on a bridge with moving traffic is dangerous and is not allowed. If you want to see the bridge up close, look for times when it is open to people on foot and follow the signs and traffic police.

**How long does it take to drive from HITEC City to Jubilee Hills?**
It depends almost entirely on traffic. The distance is only around seven kilometres, but office hours on HITEC City Road and signals on Road No. 36 can slow it down a great deal. Leave early and allow plenty of time at peak hours.

**What is the hardest part of the drive?**
For most people it is lane choice: getting into the right lane for the bridge approach near Inorbit Mall, and then handling the turns and signals around Road No. 36 and Jubilee Hills Checkpost in heavy traffic.

**Can I practise this route before driving it?**
Yes. Sawari has a free Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills route over the cable bridge that runs in a browser on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop. It is practice only and does not replace lessons.

# Necklace Road driving guide: the lakeside loop round Hussain Sagar

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/necklace-road-driving-guide.html
Category: Route guides · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Necklace Road is the lakeside road that sweeps round the western and northern shores of Hussain Sagar. It is a pleasant, mostly open drive with long bends and few junctions, but it asks for steady speed control and an eye on the median, where U-turns, buses and evening crowds can catch you out.

Here is what to expect on Necklace Road in Hyderabad, when it gets busy, the hazards worth knowing about, and how to rehearse the loop in Sawari before you drive it for real.

## What Necklace Road is like

The road follows the curve of the lake from the Khairatabad side in the south-west, up the western shore and round towards the Secunderabad side in the north-east. On one side you have the water and the lakeside parks; on the other, for much of the way, the suburban railway line, with stations such as Khairatabad, Necklace Road, Sanjeevaiah Park and James Street.

### Layout and lanes

For most of its length Necklace Road is a divided road with a median, about two lanes in each direction. That is narrower than Tank Bund Road across the lake, so overtaking a stopped bus or a slow auto needs more care. There are openings in the median for U-turns and crossings and a handful of signalled junctions.

The ground is mostly level, with only gentle rises and dips. What you notice instead are the bends: long, sweeping curves that follow the shoreline. None of them is sharp, but they are long enough that you cannot always see a stopped vehicle or a queue at a U-turn opening until you are well into the curve.

### Along the way

Necklace Road is lined with places people come to spend an evening: Sanjeevaiah Park on the north-western shore, lakeside spaces such as People's Plaza and food stalls. From the road you get long views across Hussain Sagar to the Buddha statue and the Tank Bund side. It is a lovely drive, which is exactly why other drivers slow down to look.

## When Necklace Road gets busy

Weekday mornings and evenings bring through traffic between the central offices and Secunderabad, as with most of Hyderabad traffic. But Necklace Road's busiest hours are often leisure hours: evenings, weekends and public holidays, when families, joggers and groups of friends head for the lakeside.

At those times you will find cars and two-wheelers pulling over to park, autos dropping people off, vendors near the kerb and many more people crossing. Special events and festivals around Hussain Sagar, Ganesh immersion above all, bring closures and diversions. Check Hyderabad Traffic Police (https://www.htp.gov.in) advisories if you plan to drive at festival time.

For a first drive, early morning is usually best. The road is quieter, the light is soft and you can concentrate on your lines through the bends.

## Hazards on Necklace Road

### Bends and speed

Long curves invite you to carry speed, and the open lakeside makes the road feel faster than it is. Choose your speed before the bend, keep it steady through, and look as far round the curve as you can. If you need to brake, do it while the car is still straight. Follow the posted speed limit signs; do not take your cue from whoever is overtaking you.

### U-turn openings

The median openings are where cars, autos and bikes swing round to go back the other way, sometimes slowly, sometimes from the right-hand lane without signalling, and occasionally from the left lane across your path. If you see a vehicle slowing in the right lane near an opening, assume it is about to turn. If you need to make a U-turn yourself, signal early, move to the right lane in good time and wait for a real gap. Our guide to U-turns in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/u-turns-in-hyderabad.html) explains how to do it safely.

### Buses and stopping vehicles

Buses pull in and out of stops, and with only two lanes each way, a stopped bus can take away half your road. Slow down as you approach a stop, check what is beside you before moving out, and be ready for the bus to pull out again without much warning.

### People crossing to the lake

Visitors cross Necklace Road to reach the parks and the water, often in groups and often away from crossings. Children run ahead. At night, people in dark clothing are hard to see against the lake. Slow down near parks, stalls and parked cars, which can hide someone about to step out.

### Speed breakers

There are speed breakers on and near the road, and some are poorly marked. Look for the yellow and black stripes, and for vehicles ahead dipping or braking. Slow down before the hump, not on it.

## Practical tips for Necklace Road

- **Settle into the left lane** unless you are overtaking or about to turn right. It keeps you out of the way of vehicles queuing for U-turns.

- **Leave a long gap.** On a curving road with sudden stops, a bigger gap gives you time to react.

- **Signal every move.** Indicate before lane changes, U-turns and when pulling in. Our guide to indicators and lane discipline (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/indicators-and-lane-discipline.html) covers the habits that matter most.

- **Park only where it is allowed.** Stopping on the carriageway to look at the lake is dangerous for you and for the traffic behind.

- **Take extra care after dark.** Headlights on, speed down, and expect pedestrians. See our night driving tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/night-driving-hyderabad-tips.html).

## Practise Necklace Road in Sawari

Sawari's Necklace Road route (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html#necklace-road) is a 5.0 km drive round the western and northern shores of Hussain Sagar, finishing on the Secunderabad side. It has no turns to make, so it is a good second route after Tank Bund Road: longer, narrower and with more bends to judge.

- **Start with light traffic.** Get a feel for how the car carries speed into the bends. The physics model has tyre grip and weight transfer, so braking mid-curve makes the car run wide, much as a real one would.

- **Follow the blue route band.** It shows your lane on the route. Stay inside it and left of the centre line.

- **Watch the speed limit sign** at the bottom right of the screen. Staying more than a little over it for a few seconds is logged as a speeding fault.

- **Use `Q` and `E`** for the left and right indicators whenever you change lanes or pass a stopped bus.

- **Turn the traffic up.** Once you are comfortable, set traffic to Dense. Buses stop, bikes filter through gaps and the U-turn openings start to matter.

- **Try the evening.** Choose the evening or night lighting and switch on your headlights with `L`. The lakeside looks very different with the lamps on.

Press `C` to switch between the chase view and the driver's seat; the driver's seat is better for judging bends as you really will. The car has no mirrors, so drag the mouse to look around before you change lanes. At the end, the debrief lists every fault with advice: speeding, drifting right of the centre line, leaving the road, speed breakers taken too fast and collisions, including with the median or the lake edge.

If you miss your line and end up off the route, press `R` to return to it. You can drive the Necklace Road route now (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=necklace-road), free in Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop.

## In the simulator vs the real road

The road's line, its lane counts, the median and the lake shore in Sawari come from OpenStreetMap, so the curves you practise are the real ones. Other details are estimated. Speed breakers, U-turn openings, stalls, parked vehicles, hoardings, most street lamps and many building facades are placed by rule where the map has no detail, so do not expect to find a hump or a stall in exactly the same spot on the real road. The speed limit shown in the game comes from map data; on the day, the posted sign is what counts.

Use the simulator to build habits: steady speed through bends, a good gap, early signals and an eye on the median. Then follow the real signs, signals and traffic police when you drive.

Sawari is a practice tool, not a driving course. It does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor, and its scores do not reflect any official test.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Necklace Road easy to drive?**
It is one of the gentler drives in central Hyderabad: a divided road with long, open bends and few junctions. The things to watch are buses, vehicles using the U-turn openings in the median, and people crossing to the lakeside in the evening.

**Why is it called Necklace Road?**
It curves round the shore of Hussain Sagar, and seen from above the road and its lights look like a necklace around the lake. That is the usual explanation, and the name has stuck.

**When is Necklace Road crowded?**
Evenings, weekends and holidays, when people come to the lakeside parks and food stalls. Weekday office hours also bring through traffic. Early mornings are usually the calmest time to drive it.

**Can I practise driving Necklace Road online?**
Yes. Sawari has a free 5 km Necklace Road route that runs in your browser on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop. It is for practice only and does not replace driving lessons.

# Tank Bund Road driving guide: Hyderabad's lakeside drive along Hussain Sagar

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/tank-bund-road-driving-guide.html
Category: Route guides · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Tank Bund Road is one of the easiest main roads in Hyderabad to learn on: wide, divided and nearly straight, with Hussain Sagar on one side the whole way. What makes driving on Tank Bund Road tricky is not the layout but the people on it: two-wheelers on both sides of you, buses pulling in, and walkers crossing to the lake in the evening.

This guide covers what the road is like, when it gets busy, what to look out for and how to rehearse the drive first in Sawari, the free browser driving simulator built on real Hyderabad streets.

## What Tank Bund Road is like

Tank Bund Road runs along the top of the old embankment on the eastern shore of Hussain Sagar, the large lake between Hyderabad and Secunderabad that dates back to the Qutb Shahi period. For most drivers it is simply the direct lakeside link between the two cities, and on a clear morning it is one of the nicest stretches of road in town.

### Layout and lanes

It is a divided road: a median separates the two directions, and each carriageway is wide enough for about three lanes of cars. Lane markings are there, but at busy times traffic tends to arrange itself into whatever gaps it can find, with scooters and motorbikes filling the spaces between cars. Treat the lane lines as your guide and the traffic around you as the reality.

The road is nearly level, as you would expect on top of a bund. There are no sharp bends and, if you are simply driving its length, no turns to make. You will meet a few signalled junctions near the ends and openings in the median where vehicles cross or turn back.

### Landmarks

- **The statues.** A long row of statues of Telugu historical and cultural figures stands along the lake side of the road. They are a good reminder of where you are, but they are also a reason people slow down, stop and cross.

- **The Buddha statue.** The large monolithic Buddha stands on a rock out in the lake. Driving south, it is out to your right. Enjoy it from the passenger seat; the driver's job is the road.

- **The lake promenade.** A walkway runs along the water's edge. In the evening it fills with families, couples and vendors, and many of them cross the road to reach it.

## When Tank Bund gets busy

Like most of Hyderabad traffic, Tank Bund follows the working day. Weekday mornings and evenings are the busiest times for through traffic, as people head between Secunderabad and the central offices. Midday on a weekday is usually calmer, and early weekend mornings are often the quietest of all, which makes them a sensible time for a first real drive.

Evenings are a different kind of busy. Even when traffic is moving freely, the lakeside draws crowds after sunset, especially at weekends and on holidays. Expect more people on foot, more vehicles pulling over and more two-wheelers carrying families.

The biggest disruption of the year comes during Ganesh immersion, when idols are taken to Hussain Sagar and Tank Bund is given over to processions, with diversions on the roads around the lake. The road has also been closed to traffic on some evenings for public events. Before you plan a drive at festival time or on a weekend evening, check the advisories from the Hyderabad Traffic Police (https://www.htp.gov.in).

## Hazards to watch for when driving on Tank Bund Road

### Two-wheelers on both sides

Scooters and motorbikes overtake on the left and the right, and they move between lanes without much warning. Keep a steady line and a steady speed, so they can predict you. Before you change lanes, look over your shoulder as well as in your mirror; a bike can sit in your blind spot for a long time on a road like this. Our guide to sharing the road with autos, buses and two-wheelers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) goes into more detail.

### Buses and autos stopping

Buses pull in to stops on the left and autos stop wherever a passenger waves. If you are in the left lane, expect the vehicle ahead to slow sharply or stop. Leave a bigger gap than feels necessary, and do not swerve right around a stopping bus without checking what is already coming up beside you.

### Pedestrians crossing to the lake

People cross Tank Bund away from the crossings, particularly near the statues and in the evening. They often wait in the median and step out as soon as one lane clears. Watch the median as well as the kerb, and slow down where you see groups gathering.

### Speed breakers and median openings

Speed breakers on and around the road are not always well painted. Watch for vehicles ahead dipping and braking, and slow down before the hump rather than on it. The openings in the median are where cars, autos and bikes cross or turn back, sometimes slowly and sometimes without signalling. See speed breakers and speed limits in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/speed-breakers-speed-limits-hyderabad.html) for how to take humps properly.

### The view

It sounds obvious, but the lake, the Buddha and the evening lights are distracting. The driver ahead of you may be looking at them too, and slow down for no reason you can see. Keep your eyes on the road and leave the sightseeing to your passengers.

## Practical tips for Tank Bund Road

- **Pick a lane early and stay in it.** The middle lane is usually the calmest place to settle: away from stopping buses on the left and faster traffic on the right.

- **Keep your speed steady.** Follow the posted speed limit signs rather than the fastest car around you. A smooth, predictable speed is safer with so many two-wheelers about.

- **Signal every lane change.** Indicate, check, then move. On a wide road it is easy to drift across without thinking.

- **Do not stop to look at the lake.** If you want to enjoy the view, park legally where the signs allow and walk.

- **Know where you are leaving.** Work out before you start which exit or junction you need at the far end, so you are not changing lanes at the last moment.

- **Use headlights after dusk.** Even with street lighting, the crowds and the reflections off the water make the evening harder to read.

## Practise Tank Bund Road in Sawari

Sawari's Tank Bund Road route (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html#tank-bund) is a 1.7 km southbound drive along the lake, past the statues, with Hussain Sagar on your right. It has no turns to make, so it is the route we suggest for your first drive: you can concentrate on the car and the traffic instead of the directions.

- **Choose a time and a traffic level.** Start with light traffic at midday to learn the car. Then raise the traffic level towards Dense, and try the evening or night lighting to see how the road changes.

- **Follow the blue route band.** It shows your lane on the route. Keep the car inside it and left of the centre line.

- **Practise your indicators.** Use `Q` for left and `E` for right before you move across lanes. They cancel themselves after a turn.

- **Switch views with `C`.** The chase view helps you judge where the car sits in the lane; the driver's seat view is closer to what you will really see. Drag the mouse to look around, which is a good habit to rehearse before lane changes, since the car has no mirrors.

- **Read your debrief.** At the end you get a score and a list of faults with advice: speeding, drifting right of the centre line, taking a speed breaker too fast, collisions with vehicles, pedestrians or the median, running a red light. Your best score on each route is saved in your browser.

If you drift off the route, press `R` to return to it. When you are comfortable on Tank Bund, try the longer Necklace Road loop (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/necklace-road-driving-guide.html) on the other side of the lake.

Sawari runs in Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop, with touch controls, a keyboard or a gamepad. You can start the Tank Bund drive here (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=tank-bund).

## In the simulator vs the real road

The road layout, lane counts, the median and the lake edge in Sawari come from OpenStreetMap, so the shape of the drive is real. Some details are estimated: speed breakers, U-turn openings, roadside stalls, parked vehicles, hoardings, most street lamps and many building facades are placed by rule where the map has no detail. The statues are there as a row, not as faithful likenesses. The speed limit shown in the game comes from map data and may differ from the sign on the day.

So use the simulator to practise habits: lane discipline, steady speed, signalling and watching for people. On the real road, follow the actual signs, signals and traffic police.

Sawari is for practice only. It does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor, and a good score in the game is not a measure of whether you are ready to drive on Hyderabad roads.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Tank Bund Road a good road for a new driver?**
It is one of the easier main roads in Hyderabad: wide, divided and fairly straight, with no turns needed to drive its length. The difficulty comes from two-wheelers, buses and pedestrians rather than the layout, so pick a quieter time for your first drives.

**When is Tank Bund Road busiest?**
Weekday office hours and evenings are the busiest times, and evenings and weekends bring crowds of walkers to the lakeside. During Ganesh immersion the road is taken over by processions and diversions, so check Hyderabad Traffic Police advisories before you set out.

**Can you stop on Tank Bund Road to see the lake?**
Stopping in a running lane is unsafe and can get you fined. If you want to enjoy the view, park legally where signs allow and walk along the promenade instead of slowing down or stopping on the carriageway.

**Can I practise Tank Bund Road before driving it?**
Yes. Sawari has a free Tank Bund Road route in your browser on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop. It is practice only and does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor.

# Car insurance basics in India: third-party, own damage, add-ons, no claim bonus and claims

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/car-insurance-basics-india.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

In India, third-party car insurance is compulsory by law under the Motor Vehicles Act, and it pays for harm you cause to other people and their property. A comprehensive policy adds own damage cover for your own car, and add-ons such as zero depreciation and roadside assistance extend it further.

This is a plain guide to how car insurance works in India, written for new drivers and first-time car owners, as of November 2026. We do not quote premiums or recommend any insurer. Prices depend on your car, city, age and claim history, and the policy wording, not a summary like this, decides what is covered. The insurance regulator, IRDAI (https://irdai.gov.in), publishes the rules insurers must follow.

## Is car insurance mandatory in India?

Yes, third-party insurance is mandatory for every motor vehicle used in a public place. Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes it an offence to drive, or let someone drive, a vehicle without at least third-party cover. Driving uninsured can lead to a fine and other penalties, and leaves you personally liable for any harm you cause.

- **New cars** come with long-term third-party cover. Following a Supreme Court order, new cars sold from 1 September 2018 must have three years of third-party cover, and new two-wheelers five years.

- **Own damage cover is optional by law,** although banks and finance companies usually insist on it for a car bought on a loan.

- **Your policy is on the vehicle record.** Police can check whether a car is insured against its registration number. Our Hyderabad e-challan guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-e-challan-guide.html) explains how challans reach you.

## What are third-party, own damage and comprehensive cover?

They are three building blocks: third-party covers others, own damage covers your car, and comprehensive is the two together.

| Type | What it covers | Who needs it |
|---|---|---|
| Third-party (liability) | Injury or death of other people, and damage to their property, caused by your car | Everyone, by law |
| Standalone own damage | Damage to your own car from accidents, theft, fire, floods and other listed risks | Owners who already have a separate third-party policy, such as a new car's long-term cover |
| Comprehensive | Third-party and own damage in one policy | Most owners who want their own car protected |

Standalone own damage policies have been available since 2019, so the owner of a new car with three-year third-party cover can renew just the own damage part each year. Policies also include compulsory personal accident cover for the owner-driver, unless you already have equivalent cover. Every policy has **exclusions**: claims are commonly refused for driving without a valid licence, drink driving, normal wear and tear and mechanical breakdown. Read that section before you buy.

Your licence matters to your insurance. A claim can be refused if the driver had no valid licence at the time, and there is no grace period after a licence expires. See our guide to driving licence renewal in Telangana (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-licence-renewal-telangana.html).

## Which add-ons are worth knowing about?

Add-ons are optional extras on a comprehensive or own damage policy, each for an extra premium. The common ones:

- **Zero depreciation (nil depreciation).** A normal claim deducts depreciation on replaced parts such as plastic, rubber and fibre, so you pay part of the bill. This add-on removes most of that deduction. It is popular for newer cars, and insurers usually limit it by car age and number of claims.

- **Roadside assistance.** Help if you break down: towing, a flat battery, a flat tyre, fuel delivery or a locked-out car. Useful on long highway drives.

- **Engine protection.** Covers engine damage from water entering the engine or oil leaks, which a standard policy often excludes. Worth thinking about in a city where underpasses flood in the monsoon.

- **Return to invoice.** If the car is stolen or written off, pays the gap between the insured value and the original invoice price.

- **NCB protection.** Lets you make a limited number of claims without losing your no claim bonus.

- **Consumables.** Pays for items such as engine oil, nuts and bolts and coolant used in a repair.

Choose add-ons for how and where you drive rather than buying all of them.

## How does the no claim bonus work?

The no claim bonus (NCB) is a discount on the own damage premium for every claim-free year. It does not apply to the third-party part. The standard steps are:

| Claim-free years in a row | NCB on own damage premium |
|---|---|
| 1 | 20% |
| 2 | 25% |
| 3 | 35% |
| 4 | 45% |
| 5 or more | 50% |

- **A claim resets it,** usually to zero at the next renewal, unless you have NCB protection.

- **It belongs to you, not the car.** When you sell a car and buy another, ask the insurer to transfer the NCB to the new policy.

- **Renew on time.** If your policy stays lapsed for more than 90 days, the NCB is generally lost, and driving even one day without insurance is an offence.

- **Small damage:** for a minor scrape, compare the repair bill with the NCB you would lose before claiming.

## How do you make a car insurance claim?

Tell your insurer as soon as possible, follow its steps, and keep records of everything. A typical own damage claim works like this:

- **Make the scene safe first.** Get help for anyone hurt and move out of traffic if you can. Our guide on what to do after a car accident in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/what-to-do-after-car-accident-hyderabad.html) covers the first few minutes.

- **Take photos** of the damage, the scene, number plates and any documents exchanged.

- **Inform the insurer** through its helpline or app, and note the claim number.

- **Report to the police** when someone is injured or killed, when another party's property is involved, or when the car is stolen. The insurer will ask for the FIR or report.

- **Survey.** The insurer appoints a surveyor to assess the damage. Under IRDAI rules from 2024, surveyors must be appointed quickly, and claims are to be decided within set time limits after the survey report.

- **Repair.** At a network garage, a cashless claim means the insurer pays the garage directly, minus deductibles and depreciation. Elsewhere you pay and claim reimbursement.

Claims against another driver for injury or death are a separate legal process, usually through the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, and the third-party insurer handles them. If you are unhappy with how a claim is handled, complain to the insurer first, then use IRDAI's Bima Bharosa grievance system or the Insurance Ombudsman (https://www.cioins.co.in).

## Which documents should you carry?

Carry your driving licence, registration certificate, insurance certificate and pollution under control (PUC) certificate, either as paper or in the official apps.

- **DigiLocker and mParivahan count.** Under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, as amended in 2018, and a Ministry of Road Transport and Highways advisory, documents in these two apps are treated as equal to the originals. Police can also verify your insurance against the vehicle record.

- **A photo or PDF in your gallery or email** does not have the same legal standing, so add your documents to DigiLocker or mParivahan.

- **Keep the insurer's helpline and your policy number** saved in your phone, and in the car.

Our Hyderabad traffic rules guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-traffic-rules-guide.html) covers the documents police check most often.

## Can safer driving keep insurance simpler?

Yes, in the most practical way: fewer claims mean you keep your no claim bonus and avoid the paperwork. Most small city claims come from scrapes in tight lanes, misjudged gaps, parking knocks and rear-end bumps in slow traffic.

Sawari, a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes, lets new drivers practise those situations on a phone, tablet, laptop or PC without risking a real car. The debrief lists every fault, from following too closely to drifting out of lane. It is practice only and has nothing to do with insurance cover, but calm habits built there carry over to the road.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is car insurance mandatory in India?**
Yes. Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes third-party insurance compulsory for every motor vehicle used in a public place. Own damage cover for your own car is optional, though lenders usually require it on a financed car.

**What is the difference between third-party and comprehensive insurance?**
Third-party insurance pays for injury, death or property damage you cause to others. A comprehensive policy adds own damage cover, which pays for damage to your own car from accidents, theft, fire and natural disasters, subject to the policy terms.

**What is a no claim bonus in car insurance?**
A no claim bonus is a discount on the own damage part of your premium for each claim-free year, rising in steps from 20 percent up to 50 percent after five claim-free years. It belongs to you, not the car, so you can carry it to a new car or insurer, but it is generally lost if your policy stays lapsed for more than 90 days.

**Is a digital insurance copy valid at a police check?**
Yes. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways treats documents in the DigiLocker and mParivahan apps as equal to the originals, and police can verify your policy against the vehicle record. A photo of the policy in your phone gallery does not have the same standing.

# Car maintenance checklist for India: weekly and monthly checks, monsoon prep and your PUC certificate

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/car-maintenance-checklist-puc.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

A simple car maintenance routine is a quick weekly walk-round for tyres, lights and leaks, a monthly check of tyre pressures, fluids, wipers and brakes, and the servicing your owner's manual sets out. On top of that, every car in India must carry a valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate, and from November 2026 its validity depends on the car's emission standard and age.

You do not need to be a mechanic to look after a car. Most problems that leave people stranded on a Hyderabad flyover, such as a soft tyre, a dead bulb or an overheated engine, show warning signs that a few minutes of checking would catch. Always follow your owner's manual first; this is a general checklist.

## What should you check every week?

Every week, walk round the car before you drive, look at the tyres, test the lights and glance underneath for leaks.

- **Tyres:** look for one that seems lower than the others, cuts, bulges on the sidewall, or nails in the tread.

- **Lights:** headlights (low and high beam), indicators front and back, hazard lights, brake lights and number-plate light. Ask someone to stand behind the car while you press the brake, or check the reflection in a glass door.

- **Glass and mirrors:** clean, with no cracks spreading across the windscreen.

- **Leaks:** fresh drips under the car where it was parked. Clear water under the front on a hot day is usually just the air conditioner.

- **Warning lights:** when you start the car, the dashboard lamps should come on briefly and go out. Any that stay on need attention.

## What should you check every month?

Once a month, check tyre pressures and tread, the main fluid levels, the wipers and how the brakes feel.

| Check | How | What to look for |
|---|---|---|
| Tyre pressure | With a gauge or at a fuel station air machine, tyres cold | Match the pressures on the door-frame sticker or in the manual, including the spare |
| Tyre tread | Look at the tread wear indicator bars in the grooves | Replace tyres when the tread is level with the bars, or if wear is uneven |
| Engine oil | Dipstick, engine off and cool, car on level ground | Level between the marks; top up with the grade in the manual |
| Coolant | Expansion tank markings, engine cold | Between minimum and maximum; never open a hot radiator cap |
| Brake fluid | Reservoir markings | A falling level can mean worn pads or a leak; get it checked |
| Washer fluid | Reservoir | Keep it full, especially before the dusty summer and the monsoon |
| Wipers | Run them on a wet windscreen | Streaks, juddering or split rubber mean new blades |
| Brakes | Feel while driving | Squealing, grinding, a soft pedal or the car pulling to one side |
| Battery | Look at the terminals; notice slow starting | White or green crust on the terminals, or the engine turning over slowly |

Electric cars have no engine oil or exhaust, but tyres, brakes, lights, wipers, coolant and washer fluid still need checking. See our guide to electric cars in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/electric-cars-in-hyderabad.html).

Beyond these checks, get the car serviced at the intervals in the owner's manual, by distance or by time, whichever comes first. Hyderabad's stop-start traffic and summer heat are hard on brakes, clutches and cooling systems, so do not stretch service intervals.

## How should you prepare a car for the monsoon?

Before the rains, make sure you can see, stop and grip: wipers, lights, tyres and brakes matter most.

- **Fit new wiper blades** if the old ones have been baked by the summer sun.

- **Check tyre tread.** Worn tyres cannot clear water and lose grip on wet roads.

- **Test all lights**, including fog lamps if fitted, and clean the lenses.

- **Have the brakes inspected** if they have not been looked at recently.

- **Check the demister and the air conditioner**, which clear a misted windscreen quickly.

- **Clear the drains** below the windscreen and in the sunroof, if you have one, so water does not leak into the cabin.

- **Keep a torch, an umbrella and a phone charger** in the car.

Do not drive through deep water at underpasses or low junctions. Water drawn into the engine can wreck it. Our monsoon driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/monsoon-driving-hyderabad.html) covers driving in the rain itself.

## What is a PUC certificate, and how long is it valid?

A PUC certificate shows that your vehicle's exhaust emissions were tested and found within the permitted limits. Every motor vehicle on the road must have a valid one under Rule 115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.

The validity periods were revised by the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, reported by All India Radio and the motoring press on 19 November 2026. Under the new schedule:

| Vehicle | Age from first registration | PUC validity |
|---|---|---|
| BS-VI, private (non-transport) | Up to 6 years | 3 years |
| BS-VI, private (non-transport) | Over 6, up to 10 years | 1 year |
| BS-VI, private (non-transport) | Over 10 years | 6 months |
| BS-VI, transport (taxis, goods vehicles) | Up to 6 years | 2 years |
| BS-VI, transport | Over 6, up to 10 years | 1 year |
| BS-VI, transport | Over 10 years | 6 months |
| BS-IV | Any | 6 months |
| BS-I, BS-II and BS-III | Any | 3 months |

Two details matter if you already have a certificate:

- A certificate issued before the change keeps the validity printed on it. The new periods apply from your first renewal.

- If you renew within ten days before expiry, the new certificate runs from the old expiry date, so you do not lose days by renewing early.

Before this change, the rule was one year for BS-IV and BS-VI vehicles and six months for others, and a new vehicle did not need its first test until a year after registration. Your car's emission standard is shown on the registration certificate and in the owner's manual; most cars sold in India since April 2020 are BS-VI. Because the rules have only just changed, check the date printed on your certificate rather than relying on memory.

## Where do you get a PUC certificate, and can you carry it digitally?

You get one at an authorised PUC testing centre, often at a fuel station, and you can usually check it online and show it digitally.

- Drive to an authorised PUC centre. The Parivahan PUC portal (https://puc.parivahan.gov.in/puc/) lists registered centres.

- The operator tests the exhaust with an approved analyser while the engine runs. It takes a few minutes.

- You pay the fee and receive a printed certificate with a unique number, your vehicle number and the expiry date.

A Ministry of Road Transport and Highways advisory of August 2018 told states to accept documents shown through DigiLocker or mParivahan as legally equal to the originals. Whether your PUC appears in those apps depends on your state's records, so if it does not, keep the printed certificate in the car with your other papers. The Telangana Transport Department (https://transport.telangana.gov.in) is the authority for local questions.

Driving without a valid certificate can lead to a fine, often issued as a camera or roadside e-challan. Our Hyderabad e-challan guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-e-challan-guide.html) explains how to check and pay them.

## Does Sawari help with car care?

No. Sawari is a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes, with an automatic car. It runs on a phone with an on-screen steering wheel, a tablet, a laptop or a PC, and it checks your driving, such as keep-left, indicators, signals and speed breakers. It does not model tyre wear, breakdowns or weather, so it cannot replace looking after a real car. Use it to practise the roads; use this checklist for the car. You can start on Necklace Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=necklace-road).

## Frequently asked questions

**How long is a PUC certificate valid in India?**
Under the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, reported on 19 November 2026, it depends on the emission standard and age. A private BS-VI car up to six years old gets three years, six to ten years gets one year and over ten years six months; BS-IV vehicles get six months and BS-I to BS-III three months.

**Where can I get a PUC certificate in Hyderabad?**
At any authorised PUC testing centre. Many are at fuel stations, and the Parivahan PUC portal has a list of registered centres. The test takes a few minutes and the certificate is issued straight away.

**Can I show a digital PUC certificate?**
A 2018 Ministry of Road Transport and Highways advisory says documents shown through DigiLocker or mParivahan are legally equivalent to originals. If your PUC status is not available there, carry the printed certificate.

**How often should I check my tyre pressure?**
At least once a month and before any long trip, with the tyres cold. Use the pressures on the sticker inside the driver's door frame or in the owner's manual, not the maximum printed on the tyre.

---

# Driving in Hyderabad for NRIs and visitors: licences, permits, rentals and what feels different

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-nris-and-visitors.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

Yes, NRIs and foreign visitors can drive in Hyderabad, but not on a foreign domestic licence alone: you need your home licence together with an International Driving Permit (IDP) issued in your home country, or a valid Indian driving licence. Traffic keeps to the left, and the biggest adjustment is the density and mix of vehicles rather than the rules themselves.

This guide covers the paperwork first, then renting, insurance and what driving here actually feels like. Rules are as we understand them in November 2026. Licensing is handled by the Telangana Transport Department (https://transport.telangana.gov.in) (the RTA) and national rules are set by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (https://morth.nic.in), so check with them before you rely on anything here for a long stay.

## Key facts for visitors

| Your situation | What you usually need |
|---|---|
| Foreign visitor, short stay | Home licence, an IDP issued in your home country, passport |
| NRI with a valid Indian licence | Your Indian licence (physical card or a digital copy in DigiLocker or mParivahan) |
| NRI whose Indian licence has expired | Renew it through Parivahan Sarathi and your issuing RTA before you drive |
| Foreign national living in Hyderabad | An Indian driving licence from the Telangana RTA |
| Renting a self-drive car | Whatever the rental firm asks for, which is usually stricter than the law |

India drives on the left. Cars are right-hand drive, and most rental cars at the budget end are manual, though automatics are increasingly common.

## Can a foreigner drive in Hyderabad?

Yes, with the right documents. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has stated in its published answers that an NRI or foreigner cannot drive in India merely on the basis of a foreign domestic licence. The accepted route for a visitor is an International Driving Permit, carried with the original home licence it translates.

### What an International Driving Permit is

An IDP is a booklet that translates your home licence into a standard format recognised under the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic, to which India is a party. It is not a licence on its own: it is only valid alongside your home licence.

- **Get it before you travel.** An IDP must be issued in the country that issued your licence. The Telangana RTA issues IDPs only to residents holding Indian licences, so it cannot give one to a visitor.

- **Check the format.** Some countries issue permits under more than one convention. Ask your issuing body for the one that covers India.

- **Mind the time limit.** An IDP is generally treated as valid for driving in India for up to one year, and never beyond its own expiry or the expiry of your home licence.

- **Carry everything.** Keep the IDP, the original home licence and your passport with you whenever you drive.

## Can an NRI drive in India on an Indian licence?

Yes. A valid Indian driving licence works in India regardless of where you live. The problem for many NRIs is that the licence has quietly expired while they were abroad.

- **Check the validity date** on your card or in DigiLocker before you land.

- **Renew online** through Parivahan Sarathi (https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in), choosing the state and RTA that issued it. The longer a licence has been expired, the more the RTA may ask of you, including a fresh test after a long lapse, so do not leave it.

- **Old paper licences** may need to be converted to a smart card or brought onto the national database before you can renew. Contact the issuing RTA if Sarathi cannot find yours.

Note that an Indian licence holder cannot drive in India on a foreign licence and IDP instead; the IDP system is for driving outside the country that issued your licence.

## How do I get an Indian driving licence as a foreign national?

If you are living in Hyderabad rather than visiting, plan to get an Indian licence. India does not simply swap a foreign licence for an Indian one in most cases, so expect the normal process: a learner's licence (LLR) first, then a driving test at an RTA unit.

- **Documents.** Expect to show your passport, a valid visa or residence permit for a longer stay, proof of your address in Hyderabad, photographs and your foreign licence. A short tourist visa is not suitable for this.

- **Apply online.** Applications start on Parivahan Sarathi, where you book the learner's test and later the driving test.

- **Learner's licence.** It is valid for six months, and you can take the driving test after the waiting period. Our guide to getting a driving licence in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-get-driving-licence-hyderabad.html) walks through every step.

Rules for foreign applicants differ in detail between states and have been under review nationally in 2026, with a draft proposal for a separate licence format for foreign nationals. Confirm the current document list with your RTA before you book.

## Can I rent a car in Hyderabad as a visitor?

Usually yes, but each rental company sets its own rules, and they tend to be stricter than the law. Many self-drive firms ask for an Indian licence, or a foreign licence with an IDP and a passport, and set a minimum age. Some do not rent to foreign licence holders at all, so ask before you book.

Two other options suit many visitors better. A car with a driver is widely available and removes the stress of learning the city. Ride-hailing cabs and autos cover most trips inside the city. Our guide to self-drive car rental in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/self-drive-car-rental-hyderabad.html) explains deposits, fuel, FASTag and damage checks if you do rent.

### What about insurance?

Every vehicle on Indian roads must have at least third-party insurance under the Motor Vehicles Act. A rental car or a family car will already have a policy, but you still need to check that it covers you.

- **Rental cars.** Read what the rental cover includes, the amount you pay in the event of damage, and what is excluded, such as tyres, glass or driving on unpaved roads.

- **A relative's car.** Motor policies generally cover any driver with a valid licence, but a claim can fail if your licence or permit is not valid in India. Get your papers right first.

- **Travel insurance.** Many travel policies exclude or limit driving abroad. Check yours.

## What feels different about driving in Hyderabad?

The rules are recognisable; the traffic is not. Visitors from countries with strict lane discipline usually find these the biggest adjustments:

- **Keeping left.** If you are used to the right, the hardest moments are turning onto an empty road and leaving a car park. Say "left, left" to yourself at every turn for the first few days.

- **Two-wheelers everywhere.** Motorcycles and scooters pass on both sides and fill every gap. Check mirrors constantly and change direction gently. Our guide to sharing the road with autos, buses and two-wheelers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) helps.

- **U-turns instead of right turns.** On many main roads you go past the junction and turn back at a median opening. See U-turns in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/u-turns-in-hyderabad.html).

- **Free left turns.** At some junctions you may turn left on red where a sign or arrow allows it. Never block that lane if you are going straight.

- **The horn.** It is used as a "here I am" signal more than a rebuke. A short tap is normal; long blasts are not.

- **Speed breakers.** Humps appear on main roads as well as side streets, often unmarked. Slow early.

- **Enforcement by camera.** Hyderabad issues many fines as e-challans from cameras, linked to the vehicle number. With a rental, the firm will pass them on to you.

Start with a quiet weekend morning on a wide road, such as Tank Bund or Necklace Road around Hussain Sagar, before trying the IT corridor at rush hour or the Old City lanes.

## Practise left-hand traffic in Sawari first

If you are used to driving on the right, a few practice runs before you arrive can take the edge off. Sawari is a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes: Tank Bund, Necklace Road, Charminar and Pathergatti, Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills over the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, and Banjara Hills Road No. 1. It keeps traffic to the left, includes two-wheelers, autos and buses, and gives you a debrief that lists every fault at the end of the drive.

It runs on a phone held sideways with an on-screen steering wheel, on a tablet, laptop or PC, so you can try it on the flight or at the hotel. Start with the Tank Bund route (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html#tank-bund), and once you feel settled, challenge a friend or family member to beat your score.

Sawari is for practice only. It does not replace a valid licence or permit, lessons with a licensed instructor or real experience. On the road, follow the signs, signals and instructions from the traffic police.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can a foreigner drive in Hyderabad with a foreign licence?**
Not on a foreign domestic licence alone. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways says an NRI or foreigner cannot drive in India merely on a foreign licence. Visitors normally carry their home licence together with an International Driving Permit issued in their home country, plus their passport.

**How long can I drive in India on an International Driving Permit?**
An International Driving Permit is generally accepted for up to one year, and never beyond its own expiry or that of your home licence. If you are staying longer, apply for an Indian driving licence at the Telangana RTA.

**Can an NRI drive in India with an Indian driving licence?**
Yes. An Indian licence that is still valid works in India wherever you live. If it has expired while you were abroad, renew it through the Parivahan Sarathi portal and your issuing RTA before you drive.

**Is it hard for a foreigner to drive in Hyderabad?**
It is demanding at first. Traffic keeps to the left, two-wheelers fill every gap, lane discipline is loose and U-turns replace many right turns. Most visitors find it manageable after a few calm drives at quiet times.
