# Driving licence renewal in Telangana: validity, renewing online, duplicates, address change and the IDP

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-licence-renewal-telangana.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

In Telangana you renew a driving licence on the national Parivahan Sarathi portal, and since May 2026 most renewals can be done online with Aadhaar authentication, without visiting the RTA office. Apply any time from one year before your licence expires; there is no grace period, so do not drive on an expired licence.

This guide explains how long a licence is valid, when and how to renew, and how to get a duplicate licence, change your address or apply for an international driving permit, as of November 2026. We have left out fees, because they change; the Sarathi portal shows the exact amount before you pay. If you do not have a licence yet, start with our guide to getting a driving licence in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-get-driving-licence-hyderabad.html).

## How long is a driving licence valid?

A private licence for cars and two-wheelers is valid until a set age or for a set number of years, depending on how old you are when it is issued or renewed. The rule is in Section 14 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as amended.

| Your age when the licence is issued or renewed | How long it is valid |
|---|---|
| Under 30 | Until you turn 40 |
| 30 to under 50 | Ten years |
| 50 to under 55 | Until you turn 60 |
| 55 or older | Five years |
| Transport vehicle licence (any age) | Five years (three years for vehicles carrying hazardous goods) |

A learner's licence is valid for six months. The expiry date is printed on your licence card and shown in the DigiLocker and mParivahan apps, which is the quickest way to check. In mid-2026 there were reports that the Centre was looking at longer validity, but as of November 2026 the rule above still applies.

## When should you renew, and is there a grace period?

Renew in the year before your licence expires, because there is no longer any grace period after expiry. Since the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 came into force:

- **You can apply up to one year before expiry.**

- **The old 30-day grace period is gone.** Once the date passes, you are driving without a valid licence, which is an offence and can cause problems with an insurance claim.

- **You can still renew within one year after expiry,** although a late fee may apply.

- **After more than a year,** the law allows the authority to require you to pass the test of competence again.

Put the expiry date in your phone calendar with a reminder eleven months ahead. It is the simplest way to never drive on an expired licence.

## How do you renew a driving licence online in Telangana?

Use the Driving Licence services on the Sarathi portal, choose Telangana, and pick renewal. Telangana completed its move to Sarathi across all RTA offices in 2025, and in May 2026 the Transport Department made 17 licence services available in faceless mode with Aadhaar-based authentication, including renewal, duplicate licences, replacement and changes to photo, signature and date of birth.

- Open sarathi.parivahan.gov.in (https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in), go to the driving licence services and select Telangana.

- Choose the renewal service and enter your licence number and date of birth.

- Complete Aadhaar authentication with the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile number.

- Check the details, upload what the form asks for and pay the fee online.

- Keep the application number. The renewed licence is updated in DigiLocker and mParivahan, and the card is usually posted to the address on record.

If the portal asks you to visit the RTA, for example for biometrics or a test, it lets you book a slot. The Telangana Transport Department (https://transport.telangana.gov.in) site lists the RTA offices and current notices.

### Documents, in general terms

- Your current or expired driving licence.

- Aadhaar for authentication, with your current mobile number linked.

- A recent photo and signature, if the form asks you to upload them.

- A medical certificate in Form 1A from a registered doctor if you are 40 or older, or if you hold a transport licence.

Apply only on the official Sarathi portal or at the RTA office. Agents and look-alike websites that charge extra for "fast renewal" are common, and they may misuse your Aadhaar details.

## How do you get a duplicate licence or change the address?

Both are online services on Sarathi, under the same Telangana driving licence services.

### Duplicate licence

If your licence card is lost, stolen or damaged, apply for a duplicate on Sarathi. It is one of the faceless services in Telangana. For a lost or stolen card, keep a copy of a police complaint or the declaration the form asks for. Until the duplicate arrives, the digital licence in DigiLocker or mParivahan is accepted at checks, because the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways treats documents in those two apps as equal to the originals.

### Change of address

If you have moved, apply for a change of address on the licence through Sarathi with proof of your new address. Your vehicle's registration certificate is a separate record, so update the address on the RC too, through the vehicle services on Parivahan. If you have moved to Hyderabad from another state, the RTA has asked people to update their licence details through the Parivahan portal; our guide for NRIs and visitors driving in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-nris-and-visitors.html) covers licences from elsewhere.

## How do you get an international driving permit in Hyderabad?

Apply to the Telangana RTA through Sarathi using Form 4A, if you hold a valid Indian licence and are travelling abroad. Key points:

- **Who it is for:** residents with a valid Indian licence who want to drive in another country for a short stay. It translates your Indian licence; it is not a licence on its own, so carry both.

- **Validity:** generally one year from issue, and not beyond the expiry of your Indian licence. Renew your Indian licence first if it is close to expiry.

- **What you usually need:** your licence, passport, visa or travel details where asked, photos and, in some cases, a medical certificate.

- **Visit:** unlike renewal, the permit is not in Telangana's faceless list, so expect to visit the RTA office for verification.

- **Check the destination:** some countries do not recognise the permit, or require a local licence after a period of residence. Check with that country's embassy.

## Key facts at a glance

- **Portal:** Parivahan Sarathi, Telangana selected.

- **Renewal window:** one year before expiry to one year after; no grace period for driving.

- **Faceless services:** 17 licence services online with Aadhaar since May 2026, including renewal and duplicates.

- **Over 40:** a Form 1A medical certificate is generally needed.

- **Digital copies:** licences in DigiLocker or mParivahan are valid at checks; a photo in your gallery is not.

- **IDP:** Form 4A, generally valid for one year, visit the RTA.

## Should you brush up before you renew?

A renewal does not normally need a new test, but if your licence has been expired for more than a year, or you have not driven in a long time, it helps to refresh your road sense first. Our Telangana RTA driving test tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/telangana-rta-driving-test-tips.html) list what examiners watch for.

Sawari, a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes, is a low-pressure way to get back into city habits on a phone, tablet, laptop or PC: indicating, lane discipline, U-turn openings and signals, with a debrief that lists every fault. It is practice only and does not replace lessons, a real car or the RTA test.

## Frequently asked questions

**How long is a driving licence valid in India?**
Under Section 14 of the Motor Vehicles Act, a private (non-transport) licence issued before age 30 is valid until you turn 40, one issued between 30 and 50 is valid for ten years, one issued between 50 and 55 runs until 60, and one issued at 55 or older is valid for five years. A transport licence is valid for five years.

**Is there a grace period after my driving licence expires?**
No. The old 30-day grace period was removed by the 2019 amendment, so you cannot legally drive on an expired licence. You can apply to renew from one year before expiry up to one year after it; after that, you may have to pass the driving test again.

**Can I renew my driving licence online in Telangana?**
Yes. Telangana licence services moved to the national Sarathi portal in 2025, and since May 2026 renewal is one of 17 licence services offered in faceless mode with Aadhaar authentication, so many people can renew without visiting the RTA office.

**How do I get an international driving permit in Hyderabad?**
Apply to the Telangana RTA through the Sarathi portal using Form 4A, with your valid Indian licence, passport, visa or ticket where asked, and photos. It is generally valid for one year and cannot outlast your Indian licence.

# From two-wheeler to car: driving tips for Hyderabad riders

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/two-wheeler-to-car-driving-tips.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

If you are moving from a two-wheeler to a car, your road knowledge is a head start, but you must unlearn rider habits: a car is much wider, cannot filter through gaps, has bigger blind spots and needs more room to stop. Most of the adjustment is about space and patience, not about the controls.

Hyderabad has a huge number of riders, and many eventually buy or borrow a car for the family, the monsoon or the commute. This guide is for them. It assumes you are learning the car with an instructor or a licensed driver beside you, on an LMV learner's licence; your two-wheeler licence does not cover a car.

## What carries over, and what must change?

Your knowledge of the roads carries over; your instincts about space and gaps mostly do not.

| Riding habit | Why it fails in a car | Car habit to build |
|---|---|---|
| Filtering through gaps | The car does not fit, and you block other lanes | Stay in your lane and move with the queue |
| Quick changes of direction | A car is slower to react and harder for others to read | Indicate early, then move gradually |
| Head-checks only | Pillars and the bodywork hide large areas | Mirrors first, then a shoulder check |
| Stopping at the very front | You end up over the stop line or the zebra crossing | Stop behind the line, in the queue |
| Short braking distance | A car is heavier and needs more room | Keep a bigger gap to the vehicle ahead |
| Parking in any small space | A car blocks gates, footpaths and lanes | Only marked or legal parking |

What carries over is just as important: you already read Hyderabad traffic, know how autos and buses behave, understand U-turn openings and free lefts, and know which roads flood. That makes your progress faster than someone new to the city.

## How do you judge a car's width and size?

By practising in a safe space until the car's corners feel like part of you. This is the biggest single change for riders.

- **Sit centrally in your lane.** In India you sit on the right, so most new drivers drift left towards the kerb. Keep the centre line a steady distance from your right shoulder.

- **Use markers.** In an empty space, drive slowly up to cones or a line on each side and get out to look. Notice where the line appears in your view through the windscreen.

- **Learn the front and back.** The bonnet hides a lot of road in front of you, and the boot sticks out behind. Stop short and check, rather than guessing.

- **Gaps.** If a gap only just looks wide enough, it is not. Wait.

## Mirrors and blind spots

In a car you see less around you than on a bike, so mirrors and a deliberate routine replace the quick glances you are used to.

- Before you move off, adjust the interior mirror to frame the rear window and the door mirrors so the side of the car just appears at the edge.

- Before any change of speed or direction: mirror, signal, then move.

- Before changing lanes or turning left, look over your shoulder into the blind spot. In Hyderabad, that is exactly where a scooter will be.

- The thick pillars beside the windscreen can hide a pedestrian or rider at junctions and on bends. Lean slightly to look round them.

- Before opening your door, check the mirror and look back for passing two-wheelers.

Now that you are on the other side, remember how riders behave and give them the room you once wanted. Our guide to sharing the road with autos, buses and two-wheelers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) covers it from the driver's seat.

## Lanes, not gaps: why patience matters

A car moves in lanes and queues; trying to ride it like a scooter only causes scrapes and arguments. The habits to build:

- **Pick a lane early** for the turn you want, using the painted arrows, and stay in it.

- **Do not hop lanes in a jam.** It gains almost nothing in a car.

- **Indicate before every move**, in good time. Our guide to indicators and lane discipline (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/indicators-and-lane-discipline.html) explains how early.

- **Do not block the free left** if you are going straight or right.

- **Accept being slower.** Riders who switch to a car often feel frustrated in a jam they could have ridden through. Leave earlier, put on music or a podcast, and let it go.

## Braking distances and following gaps

A car is several times heavier than a scooter, and it needs more room to stop, especially in the wet. On a bike you may be used to stopping in a very short space; in a car you cannot.

- **Keep a bigger gap.** A simple check: at a stop, you should see the rear tyres of the car in front touching the road.

- **Look further ahead.** Watch two or three vehicles ahead, and the brake lights beyond, so you can slow early and smoothly.

- **Brake progressively.** Press firmly but smoothly, rather than snatching the pedal. If the car has ABS, keep pressing in an emergency; do not pump.

- **Right foot only.** On a scooter both hands brake. In a car, one foot does accelerator and brake; on a manual the left foot is only for the clutch. If you are learning in an automatic, see our guide to driving an automatic in India (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-drive-automatic-car-india.html).

- **Allow more in the rain.** Our monsoon driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/monsoon-driving-hyderabad.html) covers wet roads.

## Parking a car, not a bike

You can no longer park on the edge of a footpath or squeeze in beside a shop. Use marked bays, pay parking, and the car parks at malls, offices and metro stations. Never park at junctions or bends, on zebra crossings, at bus stops or in front of gates. Practise reversing into a bay in a quiet car park before trying it on a busy street with people watching. Our Hyderabad parking guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-parking-guide.html) goes further.

Habits to unlearn, in one line: filtering, sudden moves, stopping over the line, short following gaps and parking wherever it fits.

## Practising the switch with Sawari

Sawari is a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes, and it treats you as a car driver: you stay in your lane, signal, stop at the line and keep your distance from traffic. The car is an automatic. It runs on a phone held sideways with an on-screen steering wheel, a tablet, a laptop or a PC.

The debrief at the end lists every fault, such as no indicator before a turn, drifting right of the centre line, red lights and collisions, so you can see which rider habits are still with you. You can also send a friend a challenge to beat your score. It is practice only, and it cannot teach width judgement the way a real car and cones can. Try Banjara Hills Road No. 1 (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=banjara-hills) with busy traffic to practise patience at junctions.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is it easier to learn a car if you already ride a two-wheeler?**
Partly. You already know the roads, the rules and how traffic behaves, which helps a lot. But some riding habits, such as filtering through gaps and changing direction quickly, have to be unlearnt because a car is much wider and slower to react.

**How do I judge the width of a car?**
Practise in an empty space with markers or cones, noting where the kerb and the lines sit in your view when the car is close to them. Over time you learn reference points on the bonnet and dashboard, and you stop drifting towards the kerb.

**Why can't I filter through traffic in a car like on a bike?**
A car is roughly two to three times as wide as a scooter, so gaps that suit a bike do not fit, and squeezing into them causes scrapes and blocks other lanes. In a car you stay in your lane and move with the queue.

**Do I need a separate licence to drive a car if I have a two-wheeler licence?**
Yes. A motorcycle licence does not cover cars. You need a light motor vehicle (LMV) class, which starts with a learner's licence for that class and a driving test in a car.

---

# How to drive an automatic car in India: P, R, N, D, hills, parking and jams

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-drive-automatic-car-india.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

To drive an automatic car, press the brake with your right foot, start the engine, move the selector from P to D, release the handbrake and ease off the brake: the car creeps forward and changes gear by itself. You use only your right foot, for both pedals, and only ever select P or R when the car is stopped.

Automatics have become common in India, from small hatchbacks to SUVs, and they make Hyderabad's stop-start traffic much less tiring. This guide covers the controls, the habits that matter and the different kinds of automatic sold in India. It is written for car drivers learning with an instructor or a licensed driver beside them.

## What do P, R, N and D mean?

They are the selector positions: Park, Reverse, Neutral and Drive. Most cars need your foot on the brake before the selector will move out of P.

| Position | What it does | When to use it |
|---|---|---|
| **P** (Park) | Locks the gearbox so the car cannot roll | When parked, with the handbrake on. Most cars start only in P or N. |
| **R** (Reverse) | Drives the car backwards | Only when fully stopped. Check all round first. |
| **N** (Neutral) | Disconnects the engine from the wheels | Being pushed or towed, or a long wait with the brake held. Never for coasting. |
| **D** (Drive) | Moves forward and changes gears automatically | Almost all normal driving |
| **M**, **+/-**, **S** or **L** | Manual, sport or low modes on some cars | Holding a lower gear on steep hills or for engine braking downhill. Check your owner's manual. |

## How do you start and stop smoothly?

Keep your right foot on the brake whenever you are stationary in D or R, and let the car's creep do the slow work.

### Moving off

- Foot firmly on the brake, then start the engine.

- Select D (or R), and wait a moment for the gear to engage.

- Release the handbrake, check mirrors and blind spot, indicate.

- Lift off the brake gently. The car creeps forward; add accelerator smoothly if you need more speed.

### Creep

Most automatics move forward slowly in D, or backwards in R, with no accelerator at all. This is called creep, and it is your best friend in slow traffic and when parking: control your speed with the brake alone. The amount of creep varies between cars and types of gearbox, so learn your car's behaviour in an empty space.

### Right foot only

Use your right foot for both pedals and rest your left foot on the floor or the footrest. Drivers who move from a manual sometimes stab at the brake with the left foot, thinking it is the clutch, which brings the car to a sudden halt. Riders moving from a scooter, where both hands brake, also need to retrain; see our two-wheeler to car tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/two-wheeler-to-car-driving-tips.html).

Never move the selector between D and R while the car is moving, and never shift into P until you have fully stopped. It can damage the gearbox and the car may lurch.

## Hills, ramps and parking

### On slopes

Automatics are easier on slopes than manuals, but some can still roll back, so keep your foot on the brake until you are ready to go.

- **Starting uphill.** Move your right foot from brake to accelerator smoothly and without delay. Many newer cars have hill-hold assist, which holds the brake for a second or two; check whether yours does. Use the handbrake if you are unsure.

- **Going downhill.** On long steep descents, a lower gear (L, 2 or manual mode) lets the engine help slow the car, so you do not overheat the brakes.

- **Basement and mall ramps.** Creep up steady, with your foot ready on the brake. Do not let the car stop and roll on a steep ramp if you can avoid it.

- **Flyover queues.** On an incline in a jam, hold the brake; do not rely on creep to hold you still.

### Parking an automatic

- Use creep and the brake to control speed as you manoeuvre. You rarely need the accelerator.

- Come to a complete stop with your foot on the brake.

- Apply the handbrake, then select P.

- Switch off the engine, and only then release the brake pedal.

Applying the handbrake before P means the car's weight rests on the brake rather than the small locking pin in the gearbox, which matters on a slope. For where to park in the city, see our Hyderabad parking guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-parking-guide.html).

## AMT, CVT, torque converter or DCT?

All four are "automatic" to drive, with P, R, N and D, but they feel different. Here is how they compare in cars sold in India, as a general guide; individual models vary.

| Type | How it works | How it feels | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AMT** (automated manual) | A manual gearbox with a computer working the clutch and gears | A noticeable pause, or "head nod", at each gear change, especially under hard acceleration | Some roll back on slopes; ease off the accelerator slightly to smooth changes |
| **CVT** (continuously variable) | Belt and pulleys give smoothly changing ratios with no fixed gears | Very smooth in traffic; engine noise can rise before the car speeds up | Feels less eager under full throttle; drive smoothly |
| **Torque converter** (AT) | A fluid coupling and planetary gears, the traditional automatic | Smooth changes and strong creep; comfortable in stop-start traffic | Usually adds cost compared with an AMT |
| **DCT** or DSG (dual-clutch) | Two computer-controlled clutches, one for odd and one for even gears | Very quick changes, sporty | Can be jerky at crawling speed; avoid holding the car on a slope with the accelerator |

For heavy city traffic, many drivers prefer the smoothness of a torque converter or CVT, while an AMT is the most affordable way into an automatic. Test drive in real traffic, not on an empty road, before you decide.

## Tips for Hyderabad traffic jams

- **Stay in D at short stops** with your foot firmly on the brake. Shifting to N at every signal gains little, and you can forget to go back to D when the light changes.

- **Use creep in a crawl.** Let the car move at walking pace on the brake rather than jumping on and off the accelerator.

- **Keep a gap.** Creep can close the gap to the car ahead faster than you expect, and two-wheelers will fill a big gap. Leave room to see the rear tyres of the car in front.

- **Never coast in N.** It gives you less control and no engine braking.

- **Long wait?** At a very long signal or a closed road, select N or P with the handbrake on, and go back to D before you need to move.

## Does your licence cover an automatic?

Yes. As of November 2026, Indian driving licences have a single light motor vehicle (LMV) class with no separate category for automatic and manual gearboxes, so an LMV licence lets you drive both.

Whether you can take the test in an automatic is less clear-cut. The central transport ministry has said that transmission need not be considered for an LMV licence, and in 2023 Kerala announced that automatic and electric cars could be used for driving tests. Practice at individual offices has varied, though, so check with the Telangana Transport Department (https://transport.telangana.gov.in) or your RTA office before booking, and see Parivahan Sarathi (https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in) for the application itself. We found no rule restricting a licence to automatics only, but if you learnt on an automatic, get some lessons in a manual before you drive one. Our RTA driving test tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/telangana-rta-driving-test-tips.html) cover the test itself.

## Practising automatic driving in Sawari

Sawari's car is an automatic, so you practise exactly what this guide describes: accelerator and brake, no clutch. To reverse, stop and hold the brake. It is a free browser simulator on five real Hyderabad routes, played on a phone held sideways with an on-screen steering wheel, on a tablet, or on a laptop or PC. The debrief at the end lists faults such as missed indicators, red lights and speeding.

It cannot teach the feel of real pedals or a real gearbox, and it is no substitute for lessons. But it is a calm place to build the habit of planning ahead in traffic. Start with Necklace Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=necklace-road).

## Frequently asked questions

**Does an LMV licence in India cover automatic cars?**
Yes. India has a single light motor vehicle (LMV) class with no separate category for automatic or manual gearboxes, so an LMV licence lets you drive both. Practise on a manual before you drive one if you learnt on an automatic.

**Can I take my driving test in an automatic car in Hyderabad?**
The central government has said transmission need not be considered for an LMV licence, but practice at individual offices has varied. Check with the Telangana Transport Department or your RTA office before you book.

**Should I use my left foot for the brake in an automatic?**
No. Use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake, and keep your left foot flat on the floor or the footrest. Using both feet risks pressing both pedals at once in an emergency.

**Should I shift to neutral at traffic signals in an automatic?**
For a normal stop at a signal, stay in D with your foot firmly on the brake. For a long wait you can select N or P with the handbrake on, but never shift to neutral while moving or rolling.

# How to park a car: reverse bay parking, parallel parking, angle parking and slopes

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-park-a-car.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

To park a car well, go slowly, use reference points on the car to judge where its corners are, and look all round before and during every movement. Reversing into a bay is usually safer than driving in forwards, parallel parking is a set sequence of steering moves, and on a slope you turn the wheels, apply the handbrake and leave the car in gear or in Park.

Parking is the manoeuvre that makes new drivers most anxious, especially with people watching. The good news is that it is a routine, not a talent. This guide gives the steps for the common types, assuming a car with the driver on the right and parking on the left, as in India. Practise in an empty car park with an instructor or a licensed driver beside you.

## What are the basics of parking any car?

Slow speed, all-round observation and reference points are the three things that make every kind of parking easier.

- **Go very slowly.** In a manual, use the clutch at the bite point; in an automatic, let the car creep on the brake. Slow speed gives you time to correct.

- **Look all round** before you start and keep looking while you move: mirrors, over both shoulders and through the rear window. Pedestrians and two-wheelers move into car parks without warning.

- **Signal** to show others what you are doing.

- **Stop and correct.** If it is going wrong, stop, pull forward and try again. Nobody is scored on parking in one go in real life.

- **Get out and look** while you are learning, to link what you saw from the seat with where the car really is.

### Using reference points without mirrors or cameras

A reference point is a part of the car that lines up with something outside, such as a bay line or the kerb, when the car is in the right place. Every car is different, so find your own with cones or chalk lines in an empty space:

- Pull up until a line on the ground meets a point on the bonnet or the bottom corner of the windscreen, then get out and check where the bumper is. That view becomes your "front bumper on the line" reference.

- Do the same for the left side: drive along a line until it appears to meet a point on the dashboard. That is your "left wheels on the line" view, useful for getting close to the kerb.

- Looking back over your left shoulder, notice where a line or the kerb appears in the rear side window when the rear wheel is level with it.

Mirrors and parking cameras are a help, not a replacement. Learn the reference points first and you can park any car, including an old one with none of the gadgets.

## How do you reverse into a parking bay?

Drive past the bay, stop when your car is two or three bays beyond it, then reverse slowly in while steering towards it and straighten up as the car lines up with the bay.

- **Position.** Drive slowly along the row about one to one-and-a-half metres from the parked cars or bay ends. Signal towards the bay.

- **Stop** when your rear bumper has passed the bay and the bay's far line is roughly level with your shoulder, or about two bay lines past the space. Adjust for your car.

- **Observe.** Check all round, especially behind and on the side away from the bay, where your front will swing out.

- **Reverse slowly and steer fully towards the bay.** Watch the nearest bay line in your mirror or over your shoulder as the car swings round.

- **Straighten up** when the car is parallel with the bay lines, by turning the wheel back the same amount you turned it.

- **Reverse straight back** until the front is inside the bay. Stop before the rear wheels reach the kerb or the end line.

- **Secure the car:** handbrake on, gear in first or reverse (manual) or Park (automatic), engine off.

If you are crooked, drive forward a little to straighten, then reverse again. Small corrections at walking pace are better than one big swing.

## How do you parallel park?

Parallel parking is a repeatable sequence: line up with the car in front, reverse until your rear wheels are level with its bumper, steer in at an angle, then steer the other way to bring the front in.

You need a space roughly one-and-a-half times your car's length while you are learning.

- **Signal left** and stop alongside the car in front of the space, level with it or slightly ahead, about half a metre to a metre away.

- **Check all round**, especially for traffic behind and two-wheelers on your left.

- **Reverse slowly and straight** until your rear wheels are level with the other car's rear bumper.

- **Steer fully left** and keep reversing slowly until your car is at about 45 degrees to the kerb. A useful check: the kerb appears in the left mirror or the left rear window at the corner.

- **Straighten the wheel** and reverse in a straight line until your front bumper clears the rear of the car in front.

- **Steer fully right** and keep reversing slowly. The front swings in towards the kerb.

- **Straighten up** as the car becomes parallel with the kerb, then move forward or back to leave room for the cars on both sides.

Check the parking is legal before you start: the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 list places where you must not park, including footpaths, pedestrian crossings, near junctions and bus stops, in front of gates and where a continuous yellow line runs along the kerb. Our Hyderabad parking guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-parking-guide.html) covers where to park in the city.

## How do you angle park?

Angle parking is the easiest: approach so the car can turn into the slanted bay in one smooth movement, and steer in once your mirror passes the near line.

- Drive along the row in the direction the bays slant, keeping a little away from the parked cars to give yourself room to turn.

- Signal and slow to walking pace.

- Start turning when your front is roughly level with the first line of the bay, or your mirror is just past it.

- Steer into the bay, then straighten up when the car is aligned with the lines.

- Stop before the kerb or wheel stop, then secure the car.

When leaving, reverse out very slowly, because you cannot see along the row until the back of the car is out. Stop and look often.

## How do you park safely on a slope?

Turn the front wheels so the car would roll into the kerb or off the road, apply the handbrake firmly and leave the car in gear or in Park.

| Situation | Front wheels | Manual gearbox |
|---|---|---|
| Downhill, with a kerb | Turned left, towards the kerb | Reverse gear |
| Uphill, with a kerb | Turned right, away from the kerb, so the tyre rests against it if the car rolls back | First gear |
| Uphill or downhill, no kerb | Turned left, towards the edge of the road | First uphill, reverse downhill |

- Stop close to the left edge and keep the footbrake pressed.

- Turn the wheels as in the table, then let the car roll gently until the tyre touches the kerb, if there is one.

- Apply the handbrake firmly.

- In a manual, select the gear in the table before switching off. In an automatic, apply the handbrake first, then select Park, so the car's weight sits on the brake rather than the gearbox.

Hyderabad has more slopes than people expect, for example the climb on Banjara Hills Road No. 1. Our guide to driving an automatic in India (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-drive-automatic-car-india.html) explains Park and the handbrake on an automatic.

## Is parking part of the RTA driving test?

Parking-type manoeuvres often are, but the details vary by office and change over time, so check with your driving school or the RTA.

Some Telangana RTA offices use test tracks with markers, and manoeuvres such as reversing or parking in a marked space may be included. We do not list a format here, because we cannot confirm one that applies everywhere. Ask your instructor what your office tests and practise exactly that. Our Telangana RTA driving test tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/telangana-rta-driving-test-tips.html) cover the rest of the test, and the Telangana Transport Department (https://transport.telangana.gov.in) has the official information.

## Can you practise parking in Sawari?

No. Sawari, a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes, does not simulate parking manoeuvres, parking bays or reversing into spaces, and it has no mirrors. It is built for driving the roads: keep-left, indicators, signals and speed breakers, with a debrief of your faults at the end. It runs on a phone with an on-screen steering wheel, a tablet, a laptop or a PC, and the car is an automatic.

Learn parking in a real car with cones in an empty space. Use Sawari for the drive to get there, for example Banjara Hills Road No. 1 (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=banjara-hills). It is practice only.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is it better to reverse into a parking space or drive in forwards?**
Reversing in is usually safer, because you drive out forwards with a clear view of passing cars and people. You reverse into the space at low speed with a good view of the bay lines, rather than reversing blind into a busy lane later.

**How do I parallel park step by step?**
Stop alongside the car in front of the space, about half a metre to a metre away. Reverse slowly until your rear wheels are level with its back bumper, steer fully left until the car is at about 45 degrees, straighten up, then steer fully right as your front clears its bumper, and straighten up close to the kerb.

**Which way should I turn my wheels when parking on a hill?**
In India, where you park on the left: facing downhill, turn the front wheels left towards the kerb. Facing uphill with a kerb, turn them right, away from the kerb, so the tyre rests against it if the car rolls back. With no kerb, turn them left towards the road edge either way. Always apply the handbrake.

**Does Sawari let you practise parking?**
No. Sawari simulates driving real Hyderabad routes with traffic, signals and speed breakers, but it does not include parking manoeuvres, reverse parking or parking bays. Parking is best learnt in a real car in an empty space with an instructor.

# Hyderabad driving FAQ: quick answers on licences, rules, roads and traffic

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-driving-faq.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

This Hyderabad driving FAQ gives short, self-contained answers to the questions people ask most about driving in the city: getting a licence from the Telangana RTA, the traffic rules and e-challans, the main roads, peak hours, safety and how to practise first. Each answer links to a fuller guide where we have one.

Answers are correct to the best of our knowledge as of November 2026. Rules, fees and fines change, so for anything official check the Telangana Transport Department (https://transport.telangana.gov.in), Parivahan Sarathi (https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in) or Hyderabad Traffic Police (https://www.htp.gov.in). We have left out fee and fine amounts on purpose.

## Licence and RTA

### How do I get a driving licence in Hyderabad?

Apply online for a learner's licence and pass its test, practise for at least 30 days, then book and pass a driving test at a Telangana RTA office. Our guide to getting a driving licence in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-get-driving-licence-hyderabad.html) covers each step.

### Where do I apply?

On the national Parivahan Sarathi (https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in) portal, choosing Telangana as your state. Fees are shown on the portal when you apply.

### How long is a learner's licence valid?

Six months from issue. You must hold it for at least 30 days before you can take the driving test, so book the test inside that window.

### What is the minimum age to drive a car?

18 years for a light motor vehicle (LMV) such as a car. The same age applies to geared motorcycles.

### Can I drive on a learner's licence alone?

No. A learner must have a person with a valid licence for that class beside them, and the car must show L plates.

### What happens in the RTA driving test?

An examiner checks that you control the car safely, follow the rules, use indicators and mirrors and complete the manoeuvres set at that office. Formats vary by office; our RTA driving test tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/telangana-rta-driving-test-tips.html) explain how to prepare.

### Does an LMV licence cover automatic cars?

Yes. India has one LMV class with no separate automatic or manual category, so an LMV licence lets you drive both. See our guide on how to drive an automatic car in India (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-drive-automatic-car-india.html).

### Can I take the test in an automatic car?

The central government has said transmission need not be considered for an LMV licence, but practice at individual offices has varied. Check with your RTA office before you book.

### Does my two-wheeler licence let me drive a car?

No. You need the LMV class added, which means a learner's licence for that class and a driving test in a car. Our two-wheeler to car tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/two-wheeler-to-car-driving-tips.html) help with the switch.

### Can visitors and NRIs drive in Hyderabad on a foreign licence?

Generally foreign visitors carry an International Driving Permit along with their home licence, and long-term residents need an Indian licence. The details depend on your situation; see our guide to driving in Hyderabad for NRIs and visitors (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-nris-and-visitors.html).

### Which documents must I carry when driving?

Your driving licence, the vehicle's registration certificate, valid insurance and a pollution under control certificate. Digital copies in the official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps are accepted.

## Rules and challans

### What do terms like LMV, PUC and free left mean?

LMV is the light motor vehicle licence class for cars, PUC is the pollution under control certificate, and a free left is a left turn allowed on red where signed. Our Hyderabad driving glossary (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-driving-glossary.html) explains many more.

### Which side of the road do you drive on in Hyderabad?

The left, as everywhere in India. Cars are right-hand drive, so you sit on the right with the centre line near your right shoulder.

### How do I check for e-challans?

Search by your vehicle number on the official Hyderabad Traffic Police e-challan site (https://echallan.tspolice.gov.in). Pay or dispute only through official channels and ignore payment links sent by text or messaging apps.

### How are most traffic offences caught?

Mostly on camera. Signal cameras, roadside cameras and officers with handheld cameras photograph the number plate, and an e-challan is raised against the registered owner.

### Can I turn left on a red signal?

Only where a free left is signed or built as a separate slip lane. Everywhere else, red means stop for every direction. Our Hyderabad traffic rules guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-traffic-rules-guide.html) explains free lefts.

### Are seat belts compulsory in the back seat?

Seat belts are meant for everyone in the car, front and back. Make sure every passenger wears one on every trip.

### Must the pillion rider wear a helmet?

Yes. Both the rider and the pillion on a two-wheeler must wear a fastened protective helmet, and Hyderabad Traffic Police enforce it for both.

### What is the drink-driving limit?

30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood, which very little alcohol can exceed. Police run regular breath tests, especially at night and weekends, so do not drink if you are driving.

### Can I use my phone while driving?

No, not held in your hand, including at a red light. Mount it for navigation, set the route before you move and pull over safely to make a call.

### What is the speed limit in Hyderabad?

There is no single city-wide figure. Limits depend on the road and are posted on signs, and they are lower near schools, hospitals and markets; see our guide to speed breakers and speed limits (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/speed-breakers-speed-limits-hyderabad.html).

### What should I do when an ambulance comes up behind me?

Move left as far as you safely can and slow down or stop to let it through. Since the 2019 Motor Vehicles Act amendments, failing to give way to an emergency vehicle is a specific offence.

### Do I need to change my TS number plate to TG?

No. TG applies to vehicles registered from March 2024, and existing TS registrations stay valid. Our guide to TG number plates (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/telangana-tg-number-plates-explained.html) has the details.

## Roads and routes

### Why are there so many U-turns instead of right turns?

On many busy roads the traffic police have closed right turns at junctions so signals can give more time to through traffic. You continue and turn back at a median opening; see U-turns in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/u-turns-in-hyderabad.html).

### What is the Outer Ring Road?

The Nehru Outer Ring Road is an eight-lane, access-controlled expressway of about 158 km around the city, with distance-based FASTag tolls. Our ORR guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-outer-ring-road-guide.html) covers exits and safety.

### What is the speed limit on the ORR?

Since 2023, 120 km/h in the two lanes nearest the median and 80 km/h in the two outer lanes. Follow the signs, which can differ near interchanges.

### Can two-wheelers and autos use the ORR?

No. Two-wheelers and three-wheelers are not allowed on the main carriageway; they can use the service roads alongside much of it.

### What is the best way to drive to the airport?

From the centre and west, most drivers use the PVNR Expressway from Mehdipatnam; from the IT corridor and outer suburbs, the ORR is usually simpler. See driving to Hyderabad airport (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-to-hyderabad-airport.html).

### Is it hard to drive near the Charminar?

Yes, it is the hardest part of the city: narrow one-way streets, heavy crowds and very little parking. Go early, or park further away and walk; see our Old City driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/charminar-old-city-driving-guide.html).

### Which roads are good for a first drive?

Wide, steady roads with few turns, such as Tank Bund Road and Necklace Road around Hussain Sagar, early in the morning. Leave busy commercial areas and the Old City until later.

### Where can I park in Hyderabad?

Use marked bays, pay parking and the car parks at malls, offices and some metro stations, never footpaths, junctions or bus stops. Our Hyderabad parking guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-parking-guide.html) goes into detail.

### Can I hire a self-drive car in Hyderabad?

Yes, several self-drive rental services operate in the city, and they generally ask for a valid licence and identity documents. See our guide to self-drive car rental in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/self-drive-car-rental-hyderabad.html).

## Traffic and timing

### What are the peak traffic hours?

As of November 2026, traffic police advisories ask commuters to avoid 8.30 to 11 am and 5 to 9 pm on affected roads. Our guide to the best time to drive in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/best-time-to-drive-in-hyderabad.html) breaks it down by area.

### When is the best time to drive?

Early morning, before about 8 am, and weekend mornings are the calmest of all. Mid-afternoon on weekdays is often lighter than the peaks.

### Which areas have the worst traffic?

The IT corridor around HITEC City, Madhapur and Gachibowli is the most often reported, along with Kukatpally, Ameerpet, Panjagutta, Mehdipatnam, LB Nagar and Secunderabad. See traffic hotspots and peak hours (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-traffic-hotspots-peak-hours.html).

### Is driving in Hyderabad hard?

It is demanding at first because of mixed traffic, two-wheelers and peak-hour jams, but wide roads and repeating patterns make it learnable. Read our honest answer (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/is-driving-in-hyderabad-hard.html) and step-by-step plan.

### Are roads closed on New Year's Eve?

Usually some are. On 31 December 2025 police closed most flyovers except Begumpet and Tolichowki, and closed Tank Bund and Necklace Road to vehicles from 11 pm to 2 am; check each year's advisory.

### Which festivals cause road closures?

Ganesh immersion closes or restricts Tank Bund, Necklace Road and NTR Marg, Bonalu brings diversions around major temples in July and August, and Ramzan nights crowd the Old City. Police publish advisories beforehand.

### Where can I find traffic advisories?

On the websites and social media of Hyderabad Traffic Police, Cyberabad Police (https://www.cyberabadpolice.gov.in) and Rachakonda Police. The Hyderabad traffic helpline quoted in 2026 advisories is 9010203626.

## Safety

### How should I deal with two-wheelers?

Expect them on both sides, check mirrors often, indicate early and change direction gradually. Our guide to sharing the road (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) covers autos and buses too.

### Is it safe to drive through a flooded road?

Only if you can see it is shallow, ideally by watching a similar car cross first. If you cannot judge the depth or the water is moving, turn back; see our monsoon driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/monsoon-driving-hyderabad.html).

### Is night driving in Hyderabad safe?

It is fine for steady drivers, with less traffic but more glare, some faster drivers and unlit hazards. Leave it until your daytime driving is confident; see our night driving tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/night-driving-hyderabad-tips.html).

### How should I take speed breakers?

Slowly enough that the car rolls over without a jolt, roughly walking to jogging pace. Expect unmarked humps on colony roads, near schools and at temple gates.

### What should I do after a minor accident?

Stop safely, switch on the hazard lights, check for injuries and call 112 for emergency help if anyone is hurt. Take photos, exchange details and inform your insurer; stay calm and avoid arguments at the roadside.

## Practising with Sawari

### What is Sawari?

Sawari is a free browser 3D driving simulator on real Hyderabad roads, built from OpenStreetMap. Traffic keeps left, the car is a right-hand-drive automatic and the drive ends with a debrief listing every fault.

### Which routes can I drive?

Five: Tank Bund Road, Necklace Road, Charminar and Pathergatti, Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills over the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, and Banjara Hills Road No. 1. See all routes (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html).

### Does it work on a phone?

Yes. Hold the phone sideways and steer with an on-screen steering wheel; it also runs on tablets, laptops and PCs, with nothing to install and no sign-up.

### Can I challenge a friend?

Yes. At the end of a drive you can send a link that challenges a friend to beat your score on the same route, time of day and traffic.

### Can Sawari replace driving lessons?

No. It helps with layouts, rules and habits such as indicating and stopping at the line, but it cannot teach real car control. Use it alongside lessons with a licensed instructor; our guide to driving simulators in India (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/free-online-driving-simulator-india.html) explains what practice on screen can and cannot do.

## Frequently asked questions

**How do I get a driving licence in Hyderabad?**
Apply online on Parivahan Sarathi for a learner's licence and pass its test, practise for at least 30 days with a licensed driver beside you, then book and pass a driving test at a Telangana RTA office. The learner's licence is valid for six months.

**How do I check e-challans in Hyderabad?**
Search by your vehicle number on the official Hyderabad Traffic Police e-challan website at echallan.tspolice.gov.in. Pay or dispute challans only through official channels and ignore payment links sent by message.

**What are the peak traffic hours in Hyderabad?**
As of November 2026, traffic police advisories ask commuters to avoid 8.30 to 11 am and 5 to 9 pm on affected roads. The IT corridor often stays busy until late at night.

**What is the drink-driving limit in India?**
The legal limit is 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood, which can be reached with very little alcohol. Hyderabad Traffic Police run regular breath tests, so the only safe plan is not to drink if you are driving.

# Is driving in Hyderabad hard? An honest answer for new drivers

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/is-driving-in-hyderabad-hard.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

Yes, driving in Hyderabad is hard at first: the traffic is dense and mixed, two-wheelers pass on both sides, many right turns are replaced by U-turns and peak hours can be slow. But it is very learnable, because the main roads are wide and the patterns repeat, and most new drivers get comfortable by building up in stages.

This is an honest look at what makes the city difficult, what makes it easier than it looks, and a plan for getting from nervous to calm. It assumes you are learning with an instructor or a licensed driver beside you.

## What makes driving in Hyderabad hard?

The difficulty comes from the mix of traffic and the amount of it, more than from the roads themselves. Here is what new drivers usually mention first.

### Mixed traffic

Cars, scooters, motorbikes, autorickshaws, city buses, cabs, delivery bikes, hand carts and pedestrians all share the same road. Each moves at a different speed and follows a different logic. You have to watch many more things at once than in a city where cars dominate.

### Two-wheelers everywhere

Two-wheelers pass on your left and your right, fill the gaps at signals and appear suddenly in your mirror. They are the single biggest source of surprises for new car drivers. Our guide to sharing the road with autos, buses and two-wheelers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) covers how to stay predictable around them.

### Autos and buses that stop anywhere

Autorickshaws pick up and drop passengers wherever they are hailed, and buses pull in and out of stops across the lane. Following too closely behind either one is a common beginner mistake.

### The U-turn system

On many busy roads the right turn at a junction has been closed. To go right, you continue and turn back at a median opening further on. It works, but it means more merging and more lane changes across fast traffic. Our post on U-turns in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/u-turns-in-hyderabad.html) explains the technique.

### Peak-hour jams and construction

Weekday mornings and evenings are slow, especially around the IT corridor. As of November 2026 Hyderabad Traffic Police advisories for the Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills flyover works ask drivers to avoid 8.30 to 11 am and 5 to 9 pm. Construction barricades narrow roads for months at a time.

### The Old City

Around the Charminar the streets are narrow, many are one-way, shops spill towards the road and crowds on foot are heavy. It is the hardest area for any driver, new or experienced.

### Monsoon rain

Heavy showers flood low junctions and underpasses, hide potholes and slow the whole city. A route that is easy in March can be stressful in a September downpour.

## What makes it easier than it looks?

Hyderabad has a lot working in a new driver's favour once you know where to look.

- **Wide arterial roads.** Many main roads are multi-lane with a central median, so there is no oncoming traffic to worry about and room for other vehicles to pass you.

- **Flyovers.** Flyovers carry through traffic over many of the worst junctions, so you can avoid a signal altogether if you choose the right lane early. See our guide to driving on flyovers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-on-flyovers-hyderabad.html).

- **The Outer Ring Road.** The ORR is an access-controlled expressway around the city with no two-wheelers or autos on the main carriageway. It is often the calmest way between outer areas.

- **Predictable patterns.** Traffic keeps left, the same junction layouts repeat across the city, and once you have done one U-turn opening or free left, the next is familiar.

- **Quiet times exist.** Early mornings, especially at weekends, are far lighter than rush hour, which gives you a gentle way in.

In the TomTom Traffic Index for 2025, Hyderabad ranked 47th among cities worldwide for congestion, behind Bengaluru and Pune. Our comparison of Hyderabad and Bengaluru traffic (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-vs-bengaluru-traffic.html) looks at the differences.

## Hard versus manageable at a glance

| Challenge | Why it feels hard | What makes it manageable |
|---|---|---|
| Two-wheelers | They pass on both sides and fill every gap | Indicate early, move gradually, check mirrors before every change of direction |
| Autos and buses | They stop without warning | Leave a bigger gap behind them and expect the stop |
| U-turns | Merging across lanes to reach the opening | Move right early and take the opening slowly |
| Peak hours | Slow, crowded and tiring | Drive outside the peaks while you are learning |
| Old City lanes | Narrow, one-way and full of people | Leave it until last and go early in the day |
| Monsoon | Flooding and hidden potholes | Avoid heavy rain until you are experienced |

## How long does it take to get comfortable?

It varies a lot from person to person, so treat this as typical experience rather than a rule. Many new drivers feel at ease on a familiar route at a quiet time within a few weeks of regular practice. Busy junctions, flyovers and peak-hour traffic usually take longer, often a few months, before they stop feeling stressful. The Old City can stay demanding for a long time, even for experienced drivers.

Three things speed it up more than anything else: driving regularly rather than once a fortnight, repeating the same routes until they feel boring, and stepping up only when the current stage feels routine. People who already ride a scooter in Hyderabad know the roads, but often need time to unlearn habits; see our tips for moving from a two-wheeler to a car (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/two-wheeler-to-car-driving-tips.html).

If a drive leaves you shaken, go back one stage for a few sessions. Confidence builds from many calm drives, not from one hard one.

## A step-by-step plan to get there

- **Get the paperwork in order.** Start with a learner's licence and lessons from a driving school or a licensed driver. Our guide to getting a driving licence in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-get-driving-licence-hyderabad.html) walks through it.

- **Learn the car in an empty space.** Moving off, stopping, slow turns and judging where the car's corners are.

- **Quiet residential roads at a quiet time.** Keeping left, indicating and simple junctions.

- **A wide, steady road early in the morning.** Tank Bund Road or Necklace Road around Hussain Sagar are good choices: few turns, a median and room to settle.

- **Signals, flyovers and U-turns outside rush hour.** Multi-lane roads such as those around HITEC City and Jubilee Hills, planning your lane before each junction.

- **Light peak traffic.** The edge of rush hour on a route you already know well.

- **The Old City last.** Early in the day, slowly, with an experienced driver beside you.

Our guide to driving in Hyderabad for beginners (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-beginners.html) goes into each stage in more detail, and our guide to the best time to drive in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/best-time-to-drive-in-hyderabad.html) helps you pick the quiet slots.

## Can a simulator help you practise first?

It can help with the layout and the habits, not with the feel of a real car. Sawari is a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes: Tank Bund Road, Necklace Road, Charminar and Pathergatti, Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills over the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, and Banjara Hills Road No. 1. Those routes follow the same order as the plan above, from easy lakeside roads to the hard Old City.

It runs on a phone held sideways with an on-screen steering wheel, on a tablet, or on a laptop or PC. The car is an automatic, traffic keeps left and you can choose how heavy the traffic is. At the end, a debrief lists every fault, from a missed indicator to a red light, and you can send a friend a challenge to beat your score on the same route.

It is practice only and does not replace lessons or the RTA test. Start with Tank Bund Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=tank-bund) in light traffic.

On a learner's licence, always drive with a licensed driver beside you and L plates on the car. Never use your phone while driving.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is driving in Hyderabad hard for beginners?**
It is demanding at first, mainly because of dense mixed traffic, two-wheelers on both sides, U-turns in place of right turns and heavy peak-hour jams. Most new drivers find it becomes manageable once they build up from quiet roads at quiet times.

**Is Hyderabad easier to drive in than Bengaluru or Mumbai?**
Many drivers find Hyderabad's wide arterial roads, flyovers and Outer Ring Road easier than older, narrower city centres, but busy areas still jam badly at peak hours. How hard it feels depends far more on where and when you drive than on the city name.

**How long does it take to get comfortable driving in Hyderabad?**
There is no fixed time. Many new drivers feel at ease on familiar routes after a few weeks of regular practice, and take a few months before busy junctions, flyovers and the Old City feel routine.

**What is the hardest part of driving in Hyderabad?**
For most people it is the two-wheelers and autos that fill every gap, combined with junctions where traffic merges from several directions. The narrow, crowded lanes of the Old City around the Charminar are the toughest area of all.

# Driving in Hyderabad for beginners: a calm guide to your first drives

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-beginners.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Driving in Hyderabad for beginners is less frightening if you build up in stages: quiet roads at quiet times first, then busier junctions and flyovers, and the narrow, crowded Old City last. This guide covers what to expect from the city's traffic and a simple order for gaining confidence.

It assumes you are learning with an instructor or a licensed driver beside you, as the law requires on a learner's licence. If you have not started the paperwork yet, see our guide to getting a driving licence in Hyderabad (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-to-get-driving-licence-hyderabad.html).

## Your first drives

The first few drives are about getting to know the car, not the city. Before you go anywhere busy:

- **Set up properly.** Seat close enough that your wrists rest on top of the wheel with your arms straight; mirrors adjusted so you can see along both sides of the car; seatbelt on before the engine starts.

- **Learn the car's size.** In an empty space, practise stopping close to a line or a marker, and notice where it sits in your view. This helps enormously later in traffic.

- **Practise smooth control.** Moving off, stopping and slow turns, until you are not thinking about your feet.

- **Keep sessions short.** Concentration fades after about an hour for most new drivers. Stop before you are tired.

India drives on the left. You sit on the right of the car, with the centre line close to your right shoulder. Many beginners drift left towards the kerb because they are not used to judging the left side of the car. Focus on the middle of your lane.

## Calmer times and areas

Hyderabad's traffic changes a lot through the day. Picking your time is the easiest way to make a drive easier.

### Times

- **Early morning** is usually calmest, particularly at weekends.

- **Weekday rush hours**, morning and evening, are hard work, especially on routes to and from the IT areas.

- **Evenings** around Hussain Sagar get busy with visitors and people walking by the lake.

- **Night** brings fewer vehicles but more glare and some faster drivers. Leave it until your daytime driving is steady; our night driving tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/night-driving-hyderabad-tips.html) cover what changes.

- **Rain** slows everything and hides potholes under water. Avoid your first drives in a heavy shower.

### Areas

Wide roads with few turns and a median are the gentlest start: you have a clear lane and no oncoming traffic to worry about. The lakeside roads around Hussain Sagar are good examples. Commercial areas with shops along the road, crowded markets and narrow residential lanes come later. The Old City around the Charminar, with its tight streets, stalls and dense crowds, is the hardest of all.

## Understanding Hyderabad traffic

### Two-wheelers

Scooters and motorbikes are everywhere, and they will pass you on both sides, sometimes in gaps you did not know existed. You cannot control that, but you can be predictable: indicate early, change direction gradually, check your mirrors before every move, and look over your shoulder before turning left, where a rider may be coming up beside you. When you stop, leave a little space so you are not boxed in.

### Autos and buses

Autorickshaws stop to pick up and drop passengers wherever they are hailed, often with little warning. Buses pull in and out of stops and need space. Hang back from both, and do not try to squeeze past a bus that is pulling out. Our guide to sharing the road with autos, buses and two-wheelers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html) goes further.

### Horns

You will hear a lot of horns. In Hyderabad traffic a short toot usually means "I am here", not anger. Do not let it rush you into a move you are not ready for. Use your own horn sparingly: a short tap to warn someone who may not have seen you, not to hurry people. Horns are prohibited in some zones, such as near hospitals, where signs say so.

### Pedestrians

People cross where they need to, not only at zebra crossings, and walk on the road where the footpath is blocked. Slow down near markets, bus stops, schools and places of worship.

## Signals, junctions and free left turns

At a signal, stop behind the stop line on red. Amber means stop unless you are too close to stop safely; it is not a cue to speed up. When the light turns green, look before you go: someone may still be crossing. Where traffic police are directing a junction, their signals override the lights.

Some Hyderabad junctions have a **free left**: you may turn left without waiting for green. Only do this where it is clearly allowed, for example by a sign, a green left arrow or a separate slip lane, and still give way to pedestrians and to traffic you are joining. Where there is no such indication, wait for the signal.

If you are going straight or turning right, do not stop in the left-most lane at a free left junction. Blocking it holds up everyone behind you, and it is a common complaint from Hyderabad drivers and the traffic police alike.

Indicate before every turn and every change of lane, in good time. Get into the correct lane early; painted arrows show which lane goes where. If you miss a turn, carry on and find the next legal U-turn rather than cutting across. See our Hyderabad traffic rules guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-traffic-rules-guide.html) for more, and the Hyderabad Traffic Police (https://www.htp.gov.in) website for official notices.

## Parking basics

- **Use proper parking**: marked bays, pay parking and the parking areas at malls and offices.

- **Do not park on footpaths**, at junctions or bends, on zebra crossings, at bus stops, in front of gates, or where signs say no parking.

- **Leave room** for others to get out, and for the car in front and behind to move.

- **Vehicles parked in the wrong place may be towed or fined.** Check the signs every time, even somewhere you have parked before.

- **Practise parking** in a quiet car park before you try it on a busy street with people waiting.

Before you get out, check your mirror and look back for two-wheelers. Opening a door into a passing scooter is an easy mistake and a dangerous one.

## A progression plan: easy roads to the Old City

Build up one step at a time. Move on only when the current stage feels routine, not just survivable.

- **An empty space.** Controls, starting, stopping, slow turns.

- **Quiet residential roads** at a quiet time. Keeping left, indicating, simple junctions.

- **Tank Bund Road and Necklace Road.** Wide, steady lakeside roads with few turns, good for lane discipline, speed control and getting used to two-wheelers around you. Go early in the day. Our Tank Bund Road guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/tank-bund-road-driving-guide.html) describes what to expect.

- **HITEC City and Jubilee Hills.** Multi-lane roads, flyovers, signals and merging traffic. Plan your lane before each junction, and start outside rush hour.

- **The Old City.** Narrow streets, crowds, stalls near the kerb, parked two-wheelers and roundabouts. Go slowly, with an experienced driver beside you, and accept that progress will be slow.

### Rehearsing the same order in a simulator

Sawari's routes (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html) follow this same order. Tank Bund Road and Necklace Road are the easy routes, Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills Road No. 1 are medium, and the Charminar and Pathergatti route is hard. It is a free browser simulator on real Hyderabad roads with left-hand traffic, local traffic and a debrief that lists every fault, from missed indicators to red lights.

It is practice only. It does not teach car control by feel, it has no mirrors, and it does not replace lessons or the official test. But driving a route on screen before you drive it for real means the layout, the turns and the busy spots are no surprise. Start with Tank Bund Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=tank-bund) and light traffic, and add more as you go.

On a learner's licence, always drive with a licensed driver beside you and L plates on the car. Do not drive tired, and never use your phone while driving.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the best time for a beginner to drive in Hyderabad?**
Early mornings, especially at weekends, are usually the calmest. Avoid weekday office rush hours, when roads around HITEC City, Gachibowli and the main corridors are at their busiest.

**What is a free left turn in Hyderabad?**
At some junctions you may turn left even when the signal is red, where a sign, a green left arrow or a separate slip lane shows it is allowed. Give way to pedestrians and traffic as you turn. Where there is no such indication, wait for the signal, and never block a free left lane if you are going straight.

**How should I deal with two-wheelers as a new driver?**
Expect them on both sides of you, check your mirrors often, indicate early and avoid sudden changes of direction. Leave space when you stop so that a rider squeezing past has room.

**Which Hyderabad roads are good for a first drive?**
Wide, steady roads with few turns, such as Tank Bund Road and Necklace Road around Hussain Sagar, at a quiet time. Leave busy commercial areas and the narrow Old City lanes until you are more confident.

# Free online driving simulator for India: does it help beginners, and what to look for

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/free-online-driving-simulator-india.html
Category: Learning to drive · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

A free online driving simulator can help a beginner in India, but only with part of the job. It is good for learning rules, building habits like indicating and keeping left, and getting used to busy traffic without risk. It cannot teach you how a real car feels, and it never replaces lessons or the official test.

This post explains where simulator practice helps, where it does not, and what makes a simulator worth your time if you are learning to drive in India. We make one, Sawari (https://sawari.airacode.online/about.html), so we will say plainly what it does and what it does not do.

## Does simulator practice help beginners?

Driving is two skills at once. One is physical: steering, braking, clutch control, judging the width of the car. The other is mental: knowing the rules, reading the road ahead, and making the right decision at the right moment. Beginners are usually overloaded because they are learning both at the same time, often in heavy traffic.

A simulator is useful for the mental side. You can rehearse the decision-making part as many times as you like, at home, without fuel, without an instructor's fee and without danger to anyone. When you get into a real car, your attention is freer for the physical side, because some of the thinking has already become routine.

It helps most with:

- **Habits**: indicating before every turn, stopping at the line on red, slowing for speed breakers.

- **Keeping left**: if you are used to games or films where traffic drives on the right, this needs re-learning.

- **Junction sense**: where to look, when to go, how signals and lanes work at a busy crossing.

- **Route familiarity**: seeing the layout of a road, its flyovers and its turns before you drive it for real.

- **Confidence**: being surrounded by autos, buses and two-wheelers stops being a shock.

## What a simulator cannot teach

Be realistic about the limits, especially with a browser simulator played on a keyboard.

- **Car control by feel.** Pressing a key is not pressing a pedal. You will not learn the clutch bite point, how firmly to brake, or how a real steering wheel loads up.

- **Judging space.** On a screen, it is harder to sense exactly where the corners of the car are. Parking and tight gaps need real practice.

- **Real consequences.** A crash in a game is a reset. On the road, it is not. A simulator should never make you braver than you are.

- **Everything people do.** No simulator captures every way real drivers, riders, pedestrians and animals behave.

- **The official test.** No simulator score counts for anything at the RTA. Only the learner's licence test and the driving test do.

Use a simulator alongside lessons with a licensed instructor, not instead of them. To drive on public roads as a learner you need a valid learner's licence, L plates and a licensed driver beside you.

## What to look for in a simulator if you are learning in India

Many driving games are built for racing or for countries that drive on the right. For learning in India, look for these things.

### Left-hand traffic and a right-hand-drive car

This is the basic requirement. You should sit on the right of the car and keep to the left of the road. Practising the other way round builds the wrong instincts.

### Local traffic

Indian traffic is mixed: autos, two-wheelers filtering through gaps, buses stopping where passengers are, people walking on the road edge. A simulator with only neat lines of cars will not prepare you for that.

### Real local roads

Generic cities teach generic skills. A simulator built on roads you will actually drive, with their real lane counts, medians, flyovers and gradients, is more useful.

### Rules feedback

The most valuable feature is honest feedback. A simulator that tells you exactly what you did wrong, such as a missed indicator or a red light, with advice on avoiding it, turns a game into practice.

### Easy to start

If it needs a powerful computer, a large download or an account, you will use it less. Free, in the browser and quick to start means you will actually open it for ten minutes between lessons.

## How Sawari fits in

Sawari is a free online driving simulator on real Hyderabad roads. Here is what it is, honestly.

### What it has

- **Five real routes**, built from OpenStreetMap and elevation data: Tank Bund Road, Necklace Road, Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills Road No. 1, and the Charminar and Pathergatti in the Old City. They run from easy to hard; the routes page (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html) has the details.

- **Left-hand traffic and a right-hand-drive car**, with a cockpit view from the driver's seat or a chase view.

- **Local traffic** from none to dense: cars, SUVs, autos, buses, mini trucks, scooters and motorbikes, plus people on the footpath. Traffic obeys the signals.

- **Guidance**: a blue band showing your lane, turn-by-turn directions with an optional voice, and a steering guide that warns you before you leave the road.

- **Rules feedback**: speeding, driving right of the centre line, wrong way on a one-way road, leaving the road, running a red light, collisions, taking a speed breaker too fast and turning without an indicator are all logged.

- **A debrief** after every drive, with a score, each fault and advice, and a personal best for each route.

- **Four times of day**, from morning to night, with headlights after dark.

The features page (https://sawari.airacode.online/features.html) covers the rest, including the dashboard and controls.

### What it does not have

- It runs on **phones, tablets, laptops and desktops**; phones and tablets are played held sideways with on-screen controls.

- You drive with **touch controls, a keyboard or a gamepad**, not a steering wheel and pedals.

- The car has an **automatic gearbox**, so there is no clutch practice.

- There are **no mirrors** and no reverse camera, so it will not train your mirror checks.

- There is no map in the car and no multiplayer.

- The routes are **not RTA test routes**, and Sawari is not affiliated with the RTA or any government body.

It needs no install and no sign-up. Your settings and best scores are saved in your own browser only. If your computer is older, the Fast graphics setting and a lower traffic level help it run smoothly.

## Getting the most out of simulator practice

A few habits make simulator time count:

- **Start easy.** Drive Tank Bund Road with light traffic until you can finish without faults. Then add traffic, then move to harder routes.

- **Read the debrief.** The point is not the score, it is the list of faults. Pick one and fix it on the next drive.

- **Drive slowly.** Drive as you would with an examiner beside you, not as fast as the game allows.

- **Use the driver's seat view.** It is closer to what you will see in a real car than the chase view.

- **Keep sessions short.** Fifteen focused minutes beats an hour of driving around.

- **Take it to your lessons.** Tell your instructor what you have been practising and ask them to check those habits in the real car.

Our guide to driving in Hyderabad for beginners (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-beginners.html) follows the same easy-to-hard order on real roads, and the RTA driving test tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/telangana-rta-driving-test-tips.html) explain how to prepare for the test itself.

When you are ready, start a drive in your browser (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html). It takes a minute to load and nothing to install.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I learn to drive using only a driving simulator?**
No. A simulator can help with road rules, habits and reading traffic, but you need lessons in a real car with a licensed instructor to learn control, and you must pass the official RTA test to get a licence.

**Is Sawari free, and do I need to install it?**
Yes, it is free and there is nothing to install. It runs in a modern browser such as Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop computer.

**Does Sawari work on a phone or tablet?**
Yes. Since version 1.6.0 phones and tablets get on-screen controls: hold the device sideways, steer with the slider on the left and use GO and BRAKE on the right. On a laptop or desktop you drive with a keyboard or a gamepad.

**Does the simulator drive on the left like in India?**
Yes. Sawari uses left-hand traffic and a right-hand-drive car, as in India, on real Hyderabad roads built from OpenStreetMap.
