# Weekend road trips from Hyderabad: where to drive and how to handle the highway

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/weekend-road-trips-from-hyderabad.html
Category: Hyderabad roads · Published 2026-11-18 · Updated 2026-11-18

The best weekend road trips from Hyderabad are all within a few hours' drive: forest hills at Ananthagiri, temples at Yadagirigutta and Srisailam, weaving villages at Pochampally, and history at Warangal and Bidar. Getting there means leaving city traffic for highways, where the speeds, the trucks and the two-lane overtaking need a different set of habits.

This guide gives rough distances and the roads you are likely to use, then the highway skills that make the drive safe. Distances are approximate and depend on where in the city you start, so check a map app for your own trip.

## Weekend road trips from Hyderabad: where to go

| Destination | Roughly how far by road | Main road out |
|---|---|---|
| Bhoodan Pochampally | about 40 to 50 km | east of the city |
| Yadagirigutta | about 60 to 65 km | the Warangal highway (NH 163) |
| Ananthagiri Hills, Vikarabad | about 75 to 90 km | the Hyderabad to Bijapur road via Chevella |
| Bidar | about 140 to 150 km | west on the Mumbai highway (NH 65) towards Zaheerabad |
| Warangal | about 145 km | the Warangal highway (NH 163) |
| Nagarjuna Sagar | about 150 to 165 km | the Nagarjuna Sagar highway via Ibrahimpatnam |
| Srisailam | about 210 to 215 km | NH 765 through the Amrabad Tiger Reserve |

### Short drives: Pochampally and Yadagirigutta

Bhoodan Pochampally, known for its ikat handloom, and the hill temple at Yadagirigutta are both east of the city and close enough for an easy half-day drive. They are good first trips if you have not driven out of Hyderabad before: you get a taste of highway speeds without hours of it. Yadagirigutta is very busy at weekends and festivals, so expect queues for parking near the temple.

### Ananthagiri Hills and Vikarabad

Ananthagiri, a few kilometres from Vikarabad town, is the nearest green hill escape, with forest, viewpoints and the Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple. The usual way is west through Moinabad and Chevella on the Hyderabad to Bijapur road. Be careful on this stretch. It has long been a narrow road with heavy truck traffic and a poor accident record, and widening work has been under way. Drive it slowly, expect diversions, and do not try to overtake in a hurry.

The last part climbs through the hills on a winding road. Take it in a low gear, keep left on the bends and watch for two-wheelers and people walking near the viewpoints.

### Warangal and Bidar

Warangal, with its fort and the Thousand Pillar Temple, is a straightforward drive on the Warangal highway, a busy national highway with plenty of trucks and buses. Bidar, just across the border in Karnataka, has a large fort and Bahmani-era monuments, reached by heading west on the Mumbai highway. Both work as long day trips, though an overnight stay lets you see them without rushing the drive home.

### Nagarjuna Sagar

The dam and reservoir at Nagarjuna Sagar are reached by leaving the city on the Outer Ring Road and taking the Nagarjuna Sagar highway through Ibrahimpatnam. Parts of the route are two-lane with villages along the way, so the drive takes longer than the distance suggests. If you are going in the monsoon to see the gates open, expect crowds and plan to park and walk.

### Srisailam and the tiger reserve

The drive to Srisailam on NH 765 is the most memorable on this list, and the one that needs the most planning. After Mannanur, the road runs for roughly 55 km through the Amrabad Tiger Reserve to the Domalapenta checkpost, with a long ghat section down towards the Krishna. Inside the reserve, vehicles are not allowed to stop on the forest road, and drivers are asked to go slowly and watch for animals crossing.

Night travel through the reserve is normally not allowed. Forest officials hold vehicles at the checkposts at night and let them continue in the morning. The rule has been relaxed for festivals such as Maha Shivaratri, and the ghat road has been closed at times after heavy rain because of landslides. Timings can change, so check with the forest department or local police before you leave, and plan to clear the forest section well before dark.

Do not stop to photograph animals, feed monkeys or step off the road inside the tiger reserve. It is unsafe for you and for the wildlife, and it is against the rules.

## Leaving and coming back to Hyderabad

The city end is often the slowest part of any road trip. Leave early on a Saturday or Sunday morning and you can be out on the highway before traffic builds. Coming back on Sunday evening is the opposite: every highway into the city fills up at the same time, and the last 20 km can take as long as the previous 100.

The Outer Ring Road helps a lot. You can use it to reach the right highway without crossing the city. Our Outer Ring Road guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-outer-ring-road-guide.html) covers joining it, lane use and exits.

## Highway driving tips for the trip

### Overtaking on two-lane roads

Many roads beyond the city are a single carriageway with one lane each way. Overtaking there is the most dangerous thing you will do on the trip.

- Overtake only where you can see a long, clear stretch ahead. Never on a bend, over a crest, near a junction or a village, or where there is a solid centre line.

- Hang back from the vehicle in front first, so you can see past it. Sitting right on a truck's bumper hides the oncoming traffic from you.

- Signal, change down a gear if you need the power, pass decisively and come back in only when you can see the overtaken vehicle in your mirror.

- If you have any doubt, do not go. Waiting a few minutes behind a slow truck costs almost nothing.

### Trucks and buses

Heavy vehicles are everywhere on these routes, day and night. Do not linger beside them, give them extra room on bends and climbs, and remember they cannot stop quickly. A truck flashing its headlights at you may be warning you, not inviting you to pass.

### Speed, villages and speed breakers

Highways pass straight through villages and towns, often with unmarked speed breakers, cattle, tractors and children near the road. Slow down well before each settlement. Our post on speed breakers and speed limits (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/speed-breakers-speed-limits-hyderabad.html) covers how to take humps safely.

### Night driving

Plan to arrive before dark where you can. Unlit highways bring glare from oncoming high beams, vehicles without working tail lights, and people and animals on the road. If you must drive at night, slow down and use dipped beams when anything is coming. See our night driving tips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/night-driving-hyderabad-tips.html) for more.

### Tolls and FASTag

National highway toll plazas run on FASTag. At the time of writing (November 2026), vehicles without a valid FASTag pay double the toll in cash or 1.25 times the toll by UPI, under rules that took effect in November 2025. Check your FASTag balance before you leave. If you drive the highways often, the NHAI's FASTag annual pass for private cars may be worth a look; check the current terms on the NHAI website (https://nhai.gov.in).

### Ghat roads and rain

On hill roads, use a lower gear going down rather than riding the brakes, keep left on blind bends and sound the horn briefly where you cannot see round the corner. In the monsoon, ghat roads can have landslides and slippery patches, so check conditions and read our monsoon driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/monsoon-driving-hyderabad.html) before you go.

### Before you set off

- Check tyres, including the spare, and the jack and wheel brace.

- Carry water, a phone charger and your licence, registration, insurance and pollution certificate (DigiLocker or mParivahan copies are fine).

- Download offline maps; signal can drop on the forest and hill sections.

- Take a break every couple of hours, and swap drivers if you can.

For opening hours, accommodation and festival dates at each destination, start with Telangana Tourism (https://tourism.telangana.gov.in).

## Where Sawari fits in

Sawari is a free browser driving simulator on five real Hyderabad routes. It has no highways, no ghat roads and no rain, so it cannot rehearse the trip itself. What it can do is build the city confidence you need for the first and last hour of every road trip: steady lane discipline, signalling, judging gaps and staying calm with buses and two-wheelers around you.

Try the longer Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills route (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html#hitec-city) with traffic set to Dense, and practise looking around with the mouse before each lane change, since the car has no mirrors. Then do your first real highway drive with an experienced driver beside you, on a short trip such as Pochampally or Yadagirigutta, before you take on Srisailam.

Sawari is for practice only. It does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor or real experience on the highway with someone experienced beside you.

## Frequently asked questions

**What are the best weekend road trips from Hyderabad?**
Popular drives include Ananthagiri Hills near Vikarabad, Yadagirigutta, Pochampally, Warangal, Bidar, Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam. The nearer ones make easy day trips; Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar are better with an overnight stay.

**Can you drive to Srisailam at night?**
Night travel through the Amrabad Tiger Reserve section between the Mannanur and Domalapenta checkposts is normally not allowed, and vehicles are held until morning. The rules have been relaxed for some festivals, so check with the forest department or local police before you set out.

**Do I need a FASTag for a road trip from Hyderabad?**
Yes, in practice. National highway toll plazas are built around FASTag. At the time of writing, vehicles without a valid FASTag pay double the toll in cash, or 1.25 times the toll if they pay by UPI.

**How do I overtake safely on a two-lane highway?**
Only overtake where you can see a long, clear stretch of road ahead, never on a bend, a crest or near a junction. Drop back first so you can see past the vehicle, signal, pass decisively, and pull back in only when you can see the overtaken vehicle in your mirror.

# What is Sawari? The free Hyderabad driving simulator, in key facts

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/what-is-sawari.html
Category: Behind the build · Published 2026-11-23 · Updated 2026-11-23

Sawari is a free 3D driving simulator that runs in a web browser and puts you on five real Hyderabad roads, from Tank Bund to the Charminar and over the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge. It plays on phones, tablets, laptops and PCs, scores every drive and explains each mistake, so new drivers can practise Hyderabad traffic before they meet it.

## Sawari at a glance

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| What is it? | A 3D driving simulator of real Hyderabad roads, in the browser |
| Cost | Free; no download, no app, no sign-up |
| Devices | Phones and tablets (held sideways), laptops and desktop PCs |
| Controls | On-screen steering wheel and pedals on touch screens; keyboard or gamepad on computers |
| Routes | Five: Tank Bund Road, Necklace Road, Charminar and Pathergatti, Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills Road No. 1 (about 18.8 km in all) |
| Traffic | Left-hand traffic and a right-hand-drive car, with cars, autos, buses, lorries, scooters and motorbikes, from none to dense |
| Feedback | A score out of 100, every fault with advice, and a personal best per route |
| Website languages | English, Hindi, Urdu and Telugu |
| Made by | AiraCode Technologies (https://airacode.online) |
| Map data | OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) and open elevation data |
| Link | sawari.airacode.online/play.html (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html) |

## Who makes Sawari?

Sawari is made by AiraCode Technologies (https://airacode.online). New versions come out often, and the release notes (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/#release-notes) list what changed in each one.

## What does the name mean?

Sawari is the Urdu word for a ride, and for a royal procession through the old city. It suits a simulator that takes you through Hyderabad's streets, from the Qutb Shahi Old City to the HITEC City flyovers.

## Which roads can you drive?

Five routes, chosen to go from easy to hard:

- **Tank Bund Road** (1.7 km, easy): the lakeside road along Hussain Sagar, with no turns. See the Tank Bund Road driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/tank-bund-road-driving-guide.html).

- **Necklace Road** (5.0 km, easy): the loop round the west and north shores of the lake. See the Necklace Road guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/necklace-road-driving-guide.html).

- **Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills** (7.4 km, medium): HITEC City Road, Inorbit Mall Road, the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, Road No. 45 and Road No. 36. See the HITEC City drive (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hitec-city-to-jubilee-hills-drive.html).

- **Banjara Hills Road No. 1** (2.6 km, medium): the climb from Masab Tank through busy junctions. See the Banjara Hills guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/banjara-hills-road-no-1-driving-guide.html).

- **Charminar and Pathergatti** (2.1 km, hard): Old City streets round the Charminar, with nine turns. See the Charminar guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/charminar-old-city-driving-guide.html).

## How realistic is it?

The road layouts, lane counts, one-way streets, flyovers, buildings, lakes, signals and places of worship come from OpenStreetMap, and the ground follows real elevation data, so slopes such as the climb up Banjara Hills Road No. 1 are real. The car has tyre grip, weight transfer, an automatic gearbox and ABS. Some things are estimated where the map has no detail: speed breakers, U-turn openings, roadside stalls, parked vehicles, hoardings and most street lamps. The behind-the-build article (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-we-built-hyderabad-in-3d.html) explains what is mapped and what is estimated.

## What does a drive check?

Each drive is marked out of 100. The debrief lists every fault with the time it happened and advice on avoiding it:

- Speeding over the limit for the road

- Driving on the wrong side of the centre line

- Going the wrong way on a one-way road

- Leaving the road

- Running a red light

- Collisions with vehicles, pedestrians, the median or walls

- Taking a speed breaker too fast

- Turning without an indicator

Spoken turn-by-turn directions guide you, in the most natural English voice your device has.

## Who is it for?

Mainly learner and new drivers in Hyderabad who want to get used to left-hand traffic, signals, indicators and local traffic before driving for real, and people who already drive but want to try an unfamiliar part of the city. It is also simply a free way to drive round Hyderabad's landmarks. Read how to make the most of it in driving in Hyderabad for beginners (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-beginners.html).

## Can you share your score?

Yes. After each drive you can share a score card picture made for WhatsApp status and Instagram Stories, or send a friend a link that challenges them to beat your score on the same route, at the same time of day and with the same traffic.

## What Sawari is not

It is not a substitute for lessons with a licensed instructor or for the RTA driving test, and it is not affiliated with the Telangana Transport Department or the traffic police. It covers five routes, not the whole city, and it has no mirrors, no weather and no multiplayer.

Start driving in your browser (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html).

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Sawari free?**
Yes. Sawari is free to play in a web browser, with no download, no app to install and no sign-up.

**Does Sawari work on mobile?**
Yes. Since version 1.6 Sawari runs on phones and tablets held sideways, with an on-screen steering wheel and GO and BRAKE pedals. On laptops and desktops you drive with a keyboard or a gamepad.

**Are Sawari's routes the real roads of Hyderabad?**
Yes. The five routes are built from OpenStreetMap road data and open elevation data, so the layouts, lanes, flyovers and gradients follow the real roads. Some details, such as shop stalls, speed breakers and most street lamps, are placed by rule where the map has no detail.

**Can Sawari replace driving lessons or the RTA test?**
No. Sawari is a practice simulator. It helps you learn habits such as keeping left and signalling, but it does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor or the official test, and it is not affiliated with the Telangana Transport Department.

# Sawari is now on phones and tablets: practise Hyderabad roads anywhere

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/play-sawari-on-phone-and-tablet.html
Category: Behind the build · Published 2026-11-19 · Updated 2026-11-19

Sawari, the free driving simulator built on real Hyderabad roads, now plays on phones and tablets as well as laptops and PCs. Open it in your browser, hold the device sideways and you are on Tank Bund, at the Charminar or crossing the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge in seconds.

Until now Sawari asked phone visitors to come back on a computer. Most people in India browse on a phone, so that shut the door on most of the people we built it for. From version 1.6.0, every device can drive.

## How to start a drive on your phone

- Open the simulator (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html) in Chrome, Safari or another modern browser.

- Pick a route. If this is your first drive, start with Tank Bund Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/tank-bund-road-driving-guide.html): it is wide, nearly straight and has no turns.

- Tap **Start driving** at the bottom of the screen.

- Hold the phone sideways. On Android the game goes full screen and stays in landscape. On an iPhone, just turn it.

There is no app to download and nothing to sign up for. Your settings and your best score on each route are kept in your browser.

## The touch controls

| Where | Control | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Bottom left | Steering wheel | Put your thumb on the wheel and turn it, as you would a real one. It turns as far as 150 degrees each way for full lock, and when you let go it spins back to the centre as the car straightens. |
| Either side of the wheel | Left and right arrows | Your indicators. They light up while they are on and cancel themselves after the turn, just like a real car. |
| Bottom right | GO | The accelerator. Hold it to drive. |
| Bottom right | BRAKE | Hold to slow down. Hold it when you are stopped to select reverse. |
| Middle of the wheel | Horn | Press and hold the centre of the steering wheel, as in a real car. |
| Top right | View, lights, back to route, pause | The eye switches between the chase view and the driver's seat. ↺ puts you back on the route if you get lost. |

Prefer the wheel on the right? Choose **Steering wheel on: Right** in the options on the start page, and the wheel and the pedals swap sides. Everything else stays where it is.

You can also drag on the open road to look around, which is handy before a lane change, since the car has no mirrors.

## Tips for a smooth drive on a phone

- **Start light.** On your first visit the phone version picks Fast graphics and Normal traffic. If your phone keeps up, try Busy or Dense traffic later.

- **Use two thumbs.** One thumb on the wheel, the other on GO and BRAKE. Rest your right thumb between the two pedals so you can switch quickly, as your foot does in a car.

- **Steer gently.** Most lane keeping needs only a small turn of the wheel. Full lock is for junctions and U-turns.

- **Signal early.** Tap the arrow before the turn, not in it. The debrief marks a missed indicator. Our guide to indicators and lane discipline (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/indicators-and-lane-discipline.html) explains why it matters on Hyderabad roads.

- **Sound on.** Spoken directions and the engine note help a lot. Tap once on the screen if you hear nothing at first; phones only start sound after a tap.

## Tablets, laptops and PCs

On an iPad or Android tablet you get the same controls, sized up for the bigger screen, with more of the road in view. On a laptop or desktop nothing changes: drive with the arrow keys or WASD, indicators on Q and E, or plug in a gamepad. A PC with a bigger screen can turn on the High graphics setting for sharp sun shadows.

## Practice, not a test

Whatever you play on, Sawari is a practice simulator. It helps you learn lane discipline, signals and the feel of real Hyderabad streets before you meet them, but it does not replace lessons with a licensed instructor or the RTA test. Read more about what a simulator can and cannot teach in our guide to free online driving simulators (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/free-online-driving-simulator-india.html).

Ready? Open Sawari on your phone (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html) and take a lap of Tank Bund.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I play Sawari on my phone?**
Yes. Open the Sawari website in your phone's browser, tap Start driving and hold the phone sideways. You steer by turning an on-screen steering wheel with your thumb and drive with GO and BRAKE pedals.

**Do I need to download an app?**
No. Sawari runs in the browser on phones, tablets, laptops and PCs. There is nothing to install and no sign-up.

**Which phones does it work on?**
It needs a reasonably recent phone with a modern browser such as Chrome or Safari. On an older or slower phone, choose Fast graphics and lighter traffic on the start page.

**Can I play in portrait?**
No. The drive needs the phone held sideways, like the view through a windscreen. If you turn the phone upright, the drive pauses and asks you to turn it back.

# How we built Hyderabad in 3D from OpenStreetMap

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-we-built-hyderabad-in-3d.html
Category: Behind the build · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Sawari's 3D Hyderabad is built from open data: the streets, flyovers and buildings come from OpenStreetMap, the hills from open elevation tiles, and everything is drawn in the browser with Three.js. This is how the pieces fit together, and where the map ends and our estimates begin.

## Starting from the map

Each of the five routes is defined by a short list of waypoints: a latitude, a longitude, the name of the road and, where it matters, the direction of travel. That last part picks the correct side of a divided road. Everything else is worked out from the map.

The script tools/fetch-osm.mjs takes those waypoints, draws a box round them with a margin of 450 metres, and asks the Overpass API for the OpenStreetMap data inside. There are several queries:

- **The main one:** every road from residential lanes up to motorways and their slip roads, buildings, lakes, parks, mapped trees and traffic signals.

- **Context:** walls and fences, metro and railway lines, stations, bus stops, petrol pumps, land use, rocks and any mapped traffic calming.

- **Names:** shops, restaurants, banks, hospitals, schools and offices that have a name, so real signboards can go on the right buildings.

The results are cached locally, so the data is only downloaded once per area. The same script fetches the elevation tiles that cover each route.

## Turning map data into a world

The heavy lifting happens in tools/build-data.mjs. It turns the raw downloads into one compact file per route, in local metres from the route's start.

### Roads and lanes

Each road is classified by its OpenStreetMap highway type. Where the map gives the number of lanes, the width or the speed limit, those are used. Where it does not, sensible defaults fill in by road class: a lane width of about 3.4 metres on main roads, narrower on colony streets, and fewer lanes on one-way roads. A check stops the traffic from trying to fit two lanes onto a road too narrow for them.

The script then builds a routing graph, finds the cheapest path through the waypoints and works out a "keep left" driving line, since India drives on the left. Turn-by-turn instructions come from the same path.

### Flyovers and bridges

OpenStreetMap marks bridges but does not usually say how high they are. So connected bridge sections are grouped, and each group is lifted 6.5 metres for each level it sits on. Very short bridges (under 80 metres in total) are treated as culverts and kept low. The ramps are then sloped smoothly from the deck down to the nearest junction. Decks span straight between their ends instead of dipping into the valley or lake below. Our flyover driving guide (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-on-flyovers-hyderabad.html) covers what that looks like from the driver's seat.

### Buildings

Building outlines come straight from the map. If a building has a mapped height or number of floors, that is used; if not, the height is estimated from the type of building, its size and the area of the city. Old City buildings are given a different character from HITEC City offices or Banjara Hills villas.

Outlines from the map and our estimated road widths do not always agree, so any building corner that pokes into a road or footpath is pushed back to the edge, and overlapping buildings are removed. Where the map has no buildings at all along a street, narrow plots are filled in on both sides, set back to the footpath and kept clear of junctions, water and parks. These filler buildings are marked as estimated.

Places of worship from the map get their own architecture, and named shops, restaurants and banks put their real names on the nearest building.

### Trees, lamps and signals

Mapped trees are kept, and parks are filled in. OpenStreetMap has very few street lamps or roadside trees mapped here, so these are laid out the way Hyderabad roads usually look: double-arm lamps on the median of divided roads about every 32 metres, single-arm lamps along the footpath on other main roads, and trees behind the footpath, never on the carriageway.

Traffic signals come from the map, but the map does not have them all. Where main roads cross near the route and nothing is mapped, the builder adds signals, starting with the biggest junctions and never within 150 metres of another signalled junction. All the signals at one junction share a cycle so they agree with each other.

## Terrain from open elevation tiles

Hyderabad is not flat. The Deccan plateau rolls, and some roads climb noticeably: Banjara Hills Road No. 1 rises about 37 metres along its route. To get this right, tools/terrain.mjs reads the Terrain Tiles (https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/) open dataset, hosted on AWS and derived from SRTM and other public sources.

The tiles store height as colour in "Terrarium" PNG images: the red, green and blue values of each pixel combine into a height in metres. The script decodes them, samples a regular grid over the area and smooths it. The source data has spikes and noise from dense buildings, so the smoothing removes those while keeping the real hills.

Then the roads are graded. Sampled on its own, each carriageway of a divided road on a hillside would come out at a different height, and side roads would drop straight off the main road. So the two halves are brought to a common height, and side roads ease out of junctions at no more than about 6 per cent.

## Rendering a low-poly city with Three.js

The game is a Three.js driving game that runs in the browser, built with Vite. The look is deliberately simple and low-poly: flat-shaded, vertex-coloured shapes, with textures only where they help, such as the asphalt and the tiled footpaths.

Performance comes from a few habits:

- **Merged geometry.** Roads, buildings and props are merged into large meshes by material, so the graphics card draws thousands of objects in a few calls.

- **Tiles.** The merged meshes are split into ground tiles a couple of hundred metres across, so only what is in view is drawn.

- **Instancing.** Repeated objects like trees, lamps and pedestrians are drawn as instances of one model.

- **Dynamic resolution.** If frames run slower than about 42 a second for a couple of seconds, the game lowers its resolution a little. The Fast graphics setting turns off sun shadows for older machines.

Time of day is a set of lighting presets for the sun, sky, fog and exposure. At night, street lamps glow and light the road beneath them, windows light up, and each vehicle gets lamps front and back.

## Traffic and people

The traffic is made of low-poly versions of the vehicle types you see on Hyderabad roads, with generic shapes and no brand styling: hatchbacks, sedans, SUVs, autos, mini trucks, buses and many scooters and motorbikes. Each AI driver plans a short path ahead, keeps a following gap, brakes comfortably to stop at red lights, slows for speed breakers and stops for people in the way. Where two paths cross, both drivers read the same decision about who goes first, so they never both go or both wait. Two-wheelers filter past slower vehicles on their right.

Real crashes come from inattention, so the AI has a small chance of a moment's distraction, which is the only way two AI drivers collide. Pedestrians walk the footpaths in outfits that shift with the area. You can read more about how this feels to drive in our post on sharing the road (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sharing-the-road-autos-buses-two-wheelers.html).

## What is mapped and what is estimated

We try to be honest about the difference. As the about page (https://sawari.airacode.online/about.html#data) sets out:

| From the map or elevation data | Estimated by rule |
|---|---|
| Roads, lanes, one-way streets, flyovers | Speed breakers and U-turn openings |
| Building outlines, heights where mapped | Facades and filler buildings |
| Lakes, parks, signals, bus stops, metro lines | Stalls, parked vehicles, hoardings |
| Places of worship, shop names, ground height | Most street lamps and roadside trees |

So the layout of a junction is real, but the stall on its corner is not. Treat the city as realistic rather than exact.

### Credit and licence

Map data is © OpenStreetMap contributors (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), available under the Open Database Licence (ODbL). The route files the game loads are a derivative database under that licence: anyone redistributing them must keep the attribution and share them under the ODbL. If a street looks wrong in the game, the best fix is often to improve OpenStreetMap itself, which helps everyone who uses it.

To see the result, drive one of the routes (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html), or look at the route list (https://sawari.airacode.online/routes.html) and the features page (https://sawari.airacode.online/features.html) first. Our free online driving simulator (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/free-online-driving-simulator-india.html) post explains what you can practise.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Sawari's 3D Hyderabad an exact copy of the city?**
No. Roads, lanes, flyovers, building outlines, signals and places of worship come from OpenStreetMap, and ground height from open elevation data. Facades, stalls, hoardings, most street lamps, speed breakers and some filler buildings are generated by rule, so they are realistic rather than exact.

**What is the game built with?**
The game uses Three.js for 3D rendering in the browser and Vite to build the site. The city data is prepared ahead of time by Node.js scripts that read OpenStreetMap data and open terrain tiles.

**Can I use OpenStreetMap data to build my own 3D city?**
Yes. OpenStreetMap data is available under the Open Database Licence, which lets you use it, including in derived data, as long as you credit OpenStreetMap contributors and share derived databases under the same licence.

**Why does the map have gaps in some areas?**
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, and coverage varies from street to street. Where buildings or other details are missing, Sawari fills in plausible ones, and the about page lists what is estimated.

# Sawari 1.8.0: a real engine note, navigation-style directions and smooth slopes

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-8-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-20 · Updated 2026-11-20

Version 1.8.0 is about how a drive sounds and feels: the car now sounds like a real small petrol car, the spoken directions talk like a navigation app, and every slope in the game rises smoothly.

## An engine that sounds like an engine

- The engine is now built from the firing of its cylinders, the way a real one makes its sound, instead of steady tones. A four-cylinder fires twice every turn of the crank: about 28 times a second at idle and 200 near the redline.

- The four cylinders are never quite equal, so the idle has the gentle, lumpy beat of a real engine and a low rumble underneath.

- It is soft and muffled when you cruise, and opens up into a harder, raspier note when you put your foot down and the revs climb.

- Browsers that cannot run it keep the previous engine sound.

## Directions like a navigation app

- The most natural voice on your device is used, Indian English first: Microsoft's natural voices on Edge, Google's voices on Chrome and Android, and Apple's on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

- Turns are announced about 500 metres out at speed, again at about 200 metres, and a few seconds before the turn itself, earlier the faster you are going.

- Distances are rounded the way navigation apps round them, and two turns close together are joined: "Turn left onto Jubilee Hills Road No. 36, then turn right."

- After a turn with a long road ahead you hear how far to keep going: "Continue on HITEC City Road for 1.2 kilometres."

- The drive starts with the direction to head in, and the engine and road noise dip while the voice speaks.

## Smooth slopes everywhere

- The ground is now shaped to the centimetre. Gentle hills used to step up in flat terraces 10 cm high; they now rise smoothly.

- Every road on the ground has a smooth profile: it still follows the hills in 4 metre steps, but the slope now changes only a tiny amount from one step to the next, so climbs like Banjara Hills Road No. 1 are even all the way up.

- Where two junctions sit close together, the road between them no longer jumps up or down: their heights are eased so that short link stays gentle.

- Flyovers and bridges keep their own ramps. Routes, turns and lengths are unchanged.

## Try it

Drive up Banjara Hills Road No. 1 (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=banjara-hills) to feel the smoother climb, or take the HITEC City route (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=hitec-city) to hear the new directions over ten turns and the cable bridge.

# Sawari 1.9.0: share your score card and challenge your friends

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-9-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-20 · Updated 2026-11-20

Version 1.9.0 turns every drive into something you can share. At the end of a route you can post a score card or send a friend a challenge to beat you on the same road.

## Your score card

- Tap **Share score card** on the results screen to make a picture sized for WhatsApp status and Instagram Stories.

- It shows the moment you arrived, straight from the game, with the route, your score and stars, your time, distance and faults.

- Add your name if you like, and the card says "Your name drove it. Can you beat it?" with the link to Sawari.

- On a phone it opens the share sheet, so you can send it to WhatsApp, Instagram or anywhere else. On a computer the picture downloads and the message is copied for you to paste.

## Challenge a friend

- Tap **Challenge a friend** to send a link with your score in it.

- Your friend's start page says who challenged them and with what score, with the same route, time of day and traffic already picked.

- When they finish, the results screen tells them who won, and they can send a challenge straight back.

- There is no account or sign-up: the challenge travels inside the link.

## Challenge links with their own preview

Added in 1.9.1: when you paste a challenge link into WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn, X or Telegram, the preview now shows that challenge's own card, with the route, the score, your name and "Can you beat it?", instead of the general Sawari picture. Tapping it still opens the game with the challenge ready.

## Share buttons right on the results screen

Added in 1.9.2: tapping **Challenge a friend** now opens a row of share buttons, like the ones at the bottom of the website: WhatsApp, Facebook, X, LinkedIn and Telegram, a caption to copy for Instagram, Copy link, and your phone's own share options.

## Try it

Drive Tank Bund Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=tank-bund), then challenge a friend to beat your score.

# Sawari 1.5.0: the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, lit flyovers, real metro piers and smoother slopes

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-5-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-19 · Updated 2026-11-19

Version 1.5.0 is about the HITEC City drive and the structures along it: the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge now looks and drives like the real one, flyovers are lit, and the metro stands on proper piers. Slopes on every route are smoother too.

## The Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge

- The two pylons now stand at either side of the lake, about 234 m apart, as on the real bridge (its main span is 233.85 m). Before, they stood close together mid-lake and were easy to miss.

- Taller white portal pylons, and stay cables you can actually see, fanned across the main span and the back spans.

- No piers in the lake under the main span: the real bridge crosses the water between its pylons with nothing below.

## Getting on and off bridges

- You can drive off the far end of the Durgam Cheruvu bridge onto Road No. 45. The car was being held back where the three-lane bridge met the two-lane road.

- Where a narrower road joins a bridge or flyover, it now tapers from the deck's width to its own over 40 m, like a real merge, instead of stepping in.

- The barrier that keeps you on a deck only pushes you back from the edge. It never stops you driving on into a slip road or the road beyond.

## Street lights on flyovers and bridges

Flyovers and bridges had no lights. They now have lamps on their parapets about every 30 m: along the outer edge of one-way decks and on both edges of two-way ones. There are about 300 on the HITEC City route alone, including the whole cable bridge.

## Metro piers

- One round pier at a time, in the middle of the median under the line, about every 30 m, as on the Hyderabad Metro. Piers no longer step sideways or stand in pairs.

- Metro stations rest on the same single round piers, without extra square columns.

- Medians under the metro are wide enough for the piers.

## Smoother slopes

Roads now follow the ground in steps of about 4 m instead of 10 m, with heights to the centimetre, so climbs like Banjara Hills Road No. 1 rise evenly instead of in visible steps.

## Ten new Hyderabad road guides

A new Hyderabad roads (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/#hyderabad-roads) section on the blog covers:

- the Outer Ring Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-outer-ring-road-guide.html) and the Regional Ring Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-regional-ring-road-rrr.html)

- the metro for drivers (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-metro-guide-for-drivers.html) and the city's flyovers and underpasses (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-flyovers-and-underpasses.html)

- driving to the airport (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-to-hyderabad-airport.html) and weekend road trips (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/weekend-road-trips-from-hyderabad.html)

- traffic hotspots and peak hours (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-traffic-hotspots-peak-hours.html) and electric cars (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/electric-cars-in-hyderabad.html)

- the history of the city's roads (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/history-of-hyderabad-roads.html) and TG number plates (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/telangana-tg-number-plates-explained.html)

## Try it

Drive Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=hitec-city) and cross the cable bridge, or try it at night to see the new lights.

# Sawari 1.6.0: play on phones and tablets

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-6-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-19 · Updated 2026-11-19

Version 1.6.0 opens Sawari to phones and tablets. Until now they saw a "use a desktop or laptop" page; now they can drive every route, with controls made for touch.

## Touch controls

- A steering slider at the bottom left: drag the knob to steer, let go and the wheel straightens. Fine near the middle, full lock at the ends.

- Left and right indicator buttons above it, lit while they are on, cancelling themselves after the turn.

- GO and BRAKE pedals at the bottom right. Hold BRAKE when stopped to select reverse, as on the keyboard.

- Horn, view, headlights, back to the route and pause at the top right.

## Made for landscape

- On Android, Start driving goes full screen and keeps the phone in landscape.

- Hold the phone upright and the drive pauses and asks you to turn it sideways.

- The speed cluster, directions and messages rearrange themselves around the controls.

## Every screen size

- Checked on small Android phones, iPhones, large phones and iPads. Tablets get bigger controls.

- On phones and tablets the Start driving button stays at the bottom of the screen while you scroll through the routes and options.

- Phones draw the city at a lighter resolution, and a phone's first visit starts with Fast graphics and Normal traffic, so drives stay smooth.

- Sound starts on your first tap, as phones require.

## Laptops and PCs

Nothing changes: keyboard and gamepad work as before.

## Try it

Read how to play Sawari on a phone or tablet (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/play-sawari-on-phone-and-tablet.html), or just open the simulator (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html) on your phone.

# Sawari 1.7.0: a real steering wheel on phones and tablets

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-7-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-19 · Updated 2026-11-19

Version 1.7.0 makes driving on a phone or tablet feel more like driving a car. The steering slider is now a steering wheel you turn with your thumb, and you can choose which side it goes.

## A steering wheel you turn

- Put your thumb on the wheel and turn it, as you would a real one. It follows your finger round.

- Full lock is 150 degrees each way; half a turn of that gives half the steering, so small corrections stay small.

- Let go and the wheel spins back to the centre as the car straightens.

- The horn is in the middle of the wheel, as in a real car: press and hold the centre to sound it. (Added in 1.7.1.)

## Indicators beside the wheel

The left and right indicators now sit on either side of the wheel, where your thumb already is. They light up while they are on and cancel themselves after the turn.

## Wheel on the left or the right

On a phone or tablet, the start page options now include **Steering wheel on**: Left (pedals on the right) or Right (pedals on the left). Only the wheel and the pedals swap; the buttons at the top, the speed cluster and the directions stay where they are. Your choice is remembered.

## Pedals set in from the edge

GO and BRAKE sit a little further in from the edges of the screen, so they are easier to reach without your thumb slipping off the side.

## Sound that stops when you do

Added in 1.7.1, on every device:

- When you reach the destination, the engine falls silent behind your debrief.

- Pausing the drive pauses the sound too, and it comes back when you resume.

- Switching to another tab or app, or turning the screen off, pauses the drive and silences it.

- Closing the tab or the browser stops all sound straight away.

## A fresh drive every time

Added in 1.7.2: every Start driving, Drive it again or Restart now begins a completely new session, built from fresh route data. A quick double tap starts one drive, not two, and coming back to the game with the browser's Back button loads it afresh instead of returning to an old, silent drive.

## Try it

Open Sawari on your phone (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html), or read how to play on a phone or tablet (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/play-sawari-on-phone-and-tablet.html).

# Sawari 1.1.0: metro pillars off the road, level carriageways and new street lights

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-1-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Version 1.1.0 fixes the metro and road problems on the HITEC City route, gives every route new street lights, makes your car's indicators easier to see and starts this blog.

## Metro pillars and stations

  - No metro pillar stands in a traffic lane any more; each one moves to the median or the footpath, or is left out.

  - Station columns stand clear of every lane, and the station deck sits high enough for buses and lorries to pass under.

  - Station name boards sit on the concourse, not hanging over the road.

## Roads on hills

  - The two halves of a divided road are level with each other, instead of one sitting a metre or two below the other on a hillside.

  - Side roads ease out of a junction rather than dropping straight off the main road.

  - The paved strip beside a road stops where a side road joins, so zebra crossings stay white stripes on the asphalt.

## People and the road

Pedestrians no longer walk along another road's carriageway or under a low flyover deck. They still cross side-road mouths, and wait for traffic when they do.

## Your car and the street

  - The indicators on your car are about twice the size and brighter when they blink.

  - New street lights on every route: a concrete plinth, a tapered pole, a swan-neck arm and an LED lantern, with double arms on medians.

## The Sawari blog

This blog launched with this version: route guides, learning to drive, road skills and how the city is built. Start with the HITEC City to Jubilee Hills drive (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hitec-city-to-jubilee-hills-drive.html), then try it in the simulator (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=hitec-city).

# Sawari 1.2.0: the HITEC City route rebuilt to match the real road

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-2-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Version 1.2.0 goes through the HITEC City route stretch by stretch and rebuilds it to match the real road: its lanes, its median, the metro above it and the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge.

## Full-width roads

The map sometimes draws the two halves of a divided road closer together than their lanes need. Sawari used to squeeze the whole road to fit its tightest spot, which shrank the three-lane bridge corridor to one lane's width. Now the two halves move apart where they crowd, so HITEC City Road keeps its four lanes each way and the bridge corridor its three, with a real median between them.

## The metro over the median

Hyderabad's metro runs above the middle of the road. The viaduct now sits over the median of HITEC City Road and Jubilee Hills Road No. 36, the median is wide enough for its pillars, and the stations span the whole road on columns in the median and on the footpaths.

## Durgam Cheruvu bridge and Road No. 45

  - The bridge and the elevated corridor keep at least 6.5 metres above the ground beneath, and about 26 metres above the lake, instead of cutting into the hills.

  - The slip roads that join the corridor rise to meet it, with no step where they join.

  - The cable-stayed pylon spans both decks, with stays fanned to each.

  - There are no U-turn openings on the bridge or the flyover.

## Smaller fixes

  - Roundabouts have a raised, planted island in the middle, like the one at Mindspace. See how to drive a roundabout (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/roundabouts-how-to-drive-india.html).

  - Bus shelters stand on the kerbside footpath, never in a median.

  - No billboards stand against a flyover deck.

## Drive it

The best way to see the difference is to drive from Cyber Towers to Jubilee Hills (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=hitec-city).

---

# Sawari 1.3.0: Hyderabad's famous buildings, smooth slopes and cleaner roads

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-3-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Version 1.3.0 puts Hyderabad's best-known buildings along the routes, with their real names and an architecture modelled on the real thing. It also makes every slope a smooth, even ride and cleans up the roads.

## Famous places, by name

Instead of a plain block, each of these now looks like itself and carries its name in English and Telugu:

| Route | Places |
|---|---|
| Tank Bund and Necklace Road | Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Telangana State Secretariat, the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar statue, the Telangana Martyrs' Memorial, the Buddha statue, Birla Mandir, Prasads IMAX, Jalavihar, Lumbini Park, NTR Gardens, Sanjeevaiah Park |
| Charminar | Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace, Salar Jung Museum, the Telangana High Court, Osmania General Hospital |
| HITEC City | Cyber Towers, Inorbit Mall, Cyber Gateway, TCS Deccan Park, ITC Kohenur, Trident, Peddamma Temple |
| Banjara Hills | GVK One, City Center Mall, Taj Krishna, Taj Deccan |

They stand on their real footprints from OpenStreetMap, are solid to drive into, and sit level on sloping ground. Read how we build the city (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/how-we-built-hyderabad-in-3d.html) for more on the map data.

## Smooth slopes

Roads used to follow every bump in the terrain data, and stepped up or down where they met another road. They are now graded into even slopes that ride smoothly. On Banjara Hills the sharp changes of grade fell from 12 to 3, and on HITEC City from 20 to 8.

## Cleaner roads

  - No more dirt showing through the asphalt: the ground now stays beneath every road, including beside flyovers.

  - One metro viaduct and one row of pillars per line. The map draws each track separately, which used to double them up.

  - Underpasses no longer lie on top of the roads above them, and the Telugu Talli Flyover now rises clear of Lower Tank Bund Road.

  - A road no longer gets a parapet instead of a footpath just because the ground beside it dips.

## Release notes

From this version on, every update gets a post like this one; the version number in the site footer links here. Drive the Old City (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=charminar) to see Mecca Masjid and Chowmahalla Palace.

---

# Sawari 1.4.0: new car sounds, a cleaner drive on every route, and themes

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-4-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-17 · Updated 2026-11-17

Version 1.4.0 is a clean-up of every route: we went over all five drives looking for anything that looked or felt wrong on the road, and fixed it. It also brings the website's light and dark themes to the simulator's start page.

## A car that sounds like a car

- A new engine sound modelled on a 1.2 litre four-cylinder: a slightly uneven idle, a deeper, rougher note under full throttle, a softer one when you lift off, and a short dip at each gear change.

- Brakes you can hear: the pads hiss harder the more you press, tyres howl and the ABS chatters in a hard stop, and the car creaks and settles as it comes to rest.

- Tyres scrub as you push through a tight bend and squeal once you go past their grip, with a pitch that wanders like real rubber. The handbrake makes them scrub too.

- Wind noise at speed, a clunk when you engage reverse, and a slightly quieter engine from the driver's seat.

## Smoother, cleaner roads

- No more patches of ground poking through the road surface, and no pale patches that looked like dirt.

- Where two roads meet at the same height they no longer flicker into each other, and sharp bends have no gaps at the corner.

- Side roads now slope gently into the main road instead of dropping or showing a dark wall along their edge.

- Zebra crossings and stop lines stop at the edge of a junction instead of painting across it.

- Footpaths and kerb strips no longer reach onto a neighbouring carriageway.

## Flyovers and bridges

- The car no longer jumps up onto a flyover when it drives underneath one, on HITEC City Road or anywhere else.

- Only real flyovers and bridges are raised. On Banjara Hills a stretch of road that climbed up to a dead end is back on the ground.

- Parapet walls no longer stand across the mouth of a ramp where it joins or leaves the main road.

- The cable-stayed bridge's cables stay within the deck.

## Scenery in the right place

- Overlapping buildings, trees inside buildings and parked vehicles inside walls have been cleared.

- Street stalls and carts stay on the kerb, never on a carriageway or a median.

- Famous buildings, like City Center Mall, step back off the road, and the plaza round the Charminar is open again.

- Lake shores on Tank Bund and Necklace Road follow the shore smoothly, and the water has less glare.

- Shop awnings sit against their buildings.

## Your theme, everywhere

If you chose light or dark on the website, the start page now opens the same way. Without a choice it follows your device's setting. There is no flash of the wrong theme while the page loads.

## A toggle on the start page

The sun and moon button next to "Back to the website" switches the theme. Your choice is remembered and shared with the website, so both stay the same.

## What stays dark

The drive itself, with its dashboard, guidance and pause screens, keeps its dark panels so they stay clear over the 3D city at any time of day. The loading screen and the "use a desktop or laptop" notice on phones follow your theme.

## Try it

Pick a theme on the website, then open the simulator (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html). New to the routes? Start with driving in Hyderabad for beginners (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/driving-in-hyderabad-for-beginners.html).

---

# Sawari 1.0.0: smarter traffic, a smoother cockpit and Necklace Road rebuilt

URL: https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/sawari-1-0-0-release-notes.html
Category: Release notes · Published 2026-11-13 · Updated 2026-11-13

Version 1.0.0 is the first numbered release of Sawari. It makes the traffic around you behave like real drivers, steadies the driver's view, adds traffic signals at busy junctions and rebuilds the surroundings of Necklace Road.

## Traffic that drives like people do

  - Cars, buses, autos and two-wheelers now look ahead along their lane and through the next junction, and keep a gap that grows with their speed.

  - Where two paths cross, the drivers settle who goes first, and the other waits instead of pushing through.

  - Two vehicles that block each other sort it out: one reverses to make room, then follows.

  - Crashes between other drivers are rare and random; the one at fault backs off and the other goes first.

  - If you stop in a lane, traffic queues, honks and then drives round you when the way is clear.

  - Pedestrians keep left, step aside for each other and wait for vehicles before crossing a side road.

## A steady driver's view

The camera in the driver's seat used the car's position from the frame before, so the dashboard shook against the road at speed. It now moves with the car exactly. Distant road markings no longer flicker in the driver's view either.

## More traffic signals

Busy junctions along every route that had no mapped signals now have them, and every signal at one junction runs on the same cycle. Signal poles stand on the kerb, never on the road. See our guide to Hyderabad's traffic rules (https://sawari.airacode.online/blog/hyderabad-traffic-rules-guide.html) for how to approach them.

## Necklace Road, as it really is

  - The lakefront stays open: no invented buildings between the road and Hussain Sagar, or squeezed against the railway.

  - The MMTS stations (Necklace Road, Sanjeevaiah Park, James Street and Khairatabad) now have platforms, shelters and name boards.

  - Trees line the railway, and parked vehicles keep off every carriageway.

## On the website

The footer now shows the version number, so you can always tell which release you are playing. Ready to try it? Drive Necklace Road (https://sawari.airacode.online/play.html?route=necklace-road).
